The next clean bracketed window is the first claim attempt.</li> </ul> </li> </ul> </li> <li><p><strong>NEG-8 drift-gate estimand ruling (2026-07-24; lead-ruled; RATIFIED in amended SCREEN+BUDGET form by the clause-10 addendum below — this original gross-only form was superseded the same day and never collected under).</strong> The whole-window drift adjudication proved the gate as previously implemented compared the two reference cells&#39; admissible envelopes at opposite corners (~0.9-1.5 J stacked) against an underived 0.05 J constant — structurally unpassable even for a physically perfect window (a8 measured point drift 0.006718 J over 2.96 h on ~38.5 J references). Ruling: the gate estimand is POINT DRIFT abs(end_point_gross − start_point_gross); the idle-subtracted point drift and the opposite-corner envelope statistic are recorded diagnostics, never gating (envelope stacking double-counts instrument uncertainty already composed into floor envelopes). The bound is DERIVED: a hash-sealed <code>joulewise.neg8_drift_bound.v1</code> artifact minted by governed CLI from a named settled-reference corpus (n&gt;=10, predeclared estimator <code>d054_point_contrast_guard_v1</code> = max(sample_range_j, t_{0.975,n-1}·s·sqrt(2))), consumed with full provenance in the verdict output. Registry addition: <code>neg8_drift_bound_underived</code> (fail-closed refusal whenever no valid governed bound artifact exists). Windows a6/a8 may be re-verdicted under the derived bound (with explicit waivers for aborted-member fragments); a5 and a7 remain refused on their genuine grounds.</p> </li> </ol> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum — debate and Ed ratification (2026-07-24).</strong> Per Ed&#39;s direction the ruling was formally debated with the peer model before ratification. The peer DISAGREED with the ruling as written on one structural point and was adjudicated correct: the point-drift statistic is the right estimand but an anomaly screen is not proof of stability — passing the gate must never erase observed drift from the claim error budget (consistent with the repo&#39;s own D-054/D-057 language). Ed RATIFIED the amended SCREEN + BUDGET design (the debate&#39;s option F, full variant, Ed explicitly directing the maximal build): per-claim-family point-drift screens (gross AND idle-subtracted, each with its own derived bound); per-family drift ALLOWANCES propagated additively into every floor/claim envelope of the window, never zero even on passing windows (allowance = max(observed excursion, derived repeatability bound)); replicated endpoint references (n=3 per endpoint, means with standard errors) and one midpoint reference prospectively, with the allowance taken over the maximum absolute excursion across sampled points; drift-bound artifacts carry a freshness horizon and re-derivation triggers (OS/build, power-supply, calibration-identity changes) with a distinct stale-bound refusal spelling; legacy pair-only windows evaluate under the single-member-endpoint minimum. Ed&#39;s recorded guardrails: watch the RIGOR SPIRAL (floors inflating past the effect sizes the science needs — monitor floor-vs-expected-effect at every extraction) and NO INVENTED PHYSICS (no functional form without a defensible basis; stated limitations beat unjustified formulas). Guiding light for all measurement-program decisions: the Splitwise replication (P2-006); methodology grounding against the Splitwise paper and comparable energy-measurement literature is in flight and feeds the collection design. Economics note recorded: Ed values artifact quality over time/tokens/machine-hours (project runs months ahead of deadline).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 2 — screen+budget wave registry + anchor-fallback gate ruling (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> Registers the wave&#39;s spellings in the D-078 closed registry: <code>neg8_idle_sub_drift_bound_underived</code>, <code>neg8_bracket_idle_sub_abs_delta_exceeded</code>, and <code>neg8_drift_bound_stale</code> (freshness horizon exceeded or re-derivation trigger fired) — the ratified clause-10 design&#39;s concrete spellings — plus <code>anchor_fallback_member_unusable</code> (unwaivable, no waiver spelling exists: a fallback-clock-anchored member may not anchor a floor or claim cell; in a floor cell it is an unwaivable re-run trigger). The latter is a LEAD-INITIATED ruling from the 2026-07-24 a7-vs-a5 prefill-scatter root cause (<code>a7_vs_a5_prefill_scatter_analysis.md</code>): a7&#39;s 11.85 J prefill &quot;floor&quot; was one fallback-anchored member (r03), half-width-zero envelope — instrument artifact (true floor ≈ 3.3–3.7 J). Flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review. Also registered (fix-round F3): <code>whole_window_drift_allowance_unrecorded</code> (passing basis-bearing verdict with no authenticated per-family allowance, or a claim missing its named allowance term — refuse, never zero; in both the floor-extraction and reducer vocabularies, mirroring <code>interpolation_bound_unrecorded</code>).</p> <p> <strong>Clause-10 addendum 3 — terminal mock bar (lead, 2026-07-24).</strong> The ratified premise &quot;mock telemetry can never bear claims&quot; had no terminal enforcement at the analysis claim boundary: honest mock members reached floor cells and claim evidence with the mock-exempted barriers disabled. Registered spelling: <code>mock_telemetry_claim_ineligible</code> (claim-bearing consumption of a member whose custody-bound config telemetry backend is the mock class; refuse — development-only evidence, no waiver spelling exists). Mockness derives from the custody-bound config (<code>hardware_target.telemetry_backend</code>, bytes bound via <code>metadata.config_sha256</code>), never from summary/metadata labels alone; where such a config exists, config/metadata/summary telemetry identities must agree by backend class (governed <code>mock:*</code> tags are mock class) or the bundle is strict-invalid. Config absence is non-production evidence (fixture-only permissive paths keep their ratified intent). Lead-initiated; flagged for Ed&#39;s PR-gate review.</p> <ol start="11"> <li><strong>Attribution-limited detection floors — Ed-RATIFIED amendment (2026-07-25).</strong> The first collection under the merged SCREEN+BUDGET rules (windows a9, a10; both whole-window verdicts PASSED) could not produce a floor: all three of a10&#39;s phase-absolute cells refuse <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code>. <strong>Finding: the instrument is ATTRIBUTION-limited, not NOISE-limited.</strong> Repeatability is 0.29-0.49 J on ~50 J points (and a settled reference pair three hours apart agreed to 0.007 J), but each member carries a clock-anchor-shift envelope of ~0.7-1.0 J: a +/-31 ms window shift across a phase boundary where power swings ~33 W mis-attributes ~1 J between prefill and decode. The composed bound is additive and measured — fiducial 24.9 ms (80-87%) plus bundle-local 3.3-6.1 ms plus edge span. Because repeatability will always beat attribution here, the refusal is STRUCTURALLY PERMANENT: no future phase corpus can pass it and there is nothing to re-collect around.</li> </ol> <p> <strong>Alternatives measured and eliminated</strong> (authenticated replay, 2026-07-25): (a) the calibration-bracket gap is NOT the cause — every cell refuses under both its minted and its post-bracket bound (delta +0.167 ms); (b) instrument tightening cannot rescue it — extraction would require a 10x (decode) to 32x (prefill) bound reduction, and each cell&#39;s bundle-local term ALONE (3.3-6.1 ms) already exceeds the entire required bound (0.99-2.9 ms), so even a perfect fiducial calibration would still refuse; (c) coarser granularity does not rescue it — request-level cells replayed on a10 and a8 have smaller envelopes (1.5-1.9 J) but still dominate and still refuse; (d) an ABBA common-mode estimator gives a real 3x gain (a5 decode 6.46 J -&gt; 2.13 J) but remains above that cell&#39;s 0.60 J point floor. The labelled path below is therefore not the preferred option among several — it is the only remaining path to any detection floor at all, at any granularity, on this instrument.</p> <p> <strong>Ruling (Ed-ratified).</strong> D-054 registers the detection floor as a practical prediction bound on FALSE OBSERVED EFFECTS, not as a repeatability statistic; a false observed effect may arise from scatter OR from anchor mis-attribution, and the corner-widened maximum is exactly the largest false effect this instrument can produce. <code>admissible_set_uncertainty_dominates_point_floor</code> therefore becomes a LABELLED CLAIM PATH rather than a hard refusal: extraction publishes the widened floor with a <code>floor_source</code> field naming the dominant term (here <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>) and retains the point floor separately as the repeatability diagnostic. The gate keeps its real function — preventing a repeatability-only number from publishing as if it were the whole story — while no longer conflating &quot;unsound corpus&quot; with &quot;instrument-limited floor&quot;. a10 is sound.</p> <p> <strong>Binding condition — SINGLE-COUNT DISCIPLINE (Ed: &quot;the cost seems sensible as long as it&#39;s noted&quot;).</strong> The floor gate now contains the anchor term, and each claim&#39;s decision interval separately consumes the member&#39;s <code>E_clock_anchor_shift_bound_j</code>. These are different objects (calibration false-effect bound vs claim-side measurement uncertainty) and both are legitimate, but the consequence is that the effective clearable effect is FLOOR + CLAIM-SIDE BOUND (~5 J for phase contrasts), not the floor alone. Every artifact publishing an attribution-limited floor must state this explicitly so that neither term is later removed as an apparent double count. Science must be sized to the ~5 J bar; Splitwise-class effects (tens of percent of tens of joules) clear it with margin.</p> <p> <strong>Not authorised by this amendment:</strong> any instrument-tightening program. Revisit only if a pilot shows target effects below ~3x the widened floor. The free lever is workload sizing — attribution error is approximately duration-independent while effects scale with workload, so longer prefill/decode raises effect-to-floor linearly at zero instrument cost (queue FLOOR-WORKLOAD-SIZING-01).</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <strong aria-current="page">Recent</strong> · <a href="decision_log_archive_1.html">Archive 1</a></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

./docs/site/claims_ladder.html:1:<!DOCTYPE html> <html lang="en"> <head> <meta charset="utf-8"> <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> <title>Claims Ladder - JouleWise</title> <script>document.documentElement.classList.add("js-enabled");</script> <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 100 100'><text y='.9em' font-size='90'>⚡</text></svg>"> </head> <body> <header class="site"> <nav class="nav"> <a class="brand" href="index.html"><span class="dot"></span>JOULEWISE</a> <div class="links"> <a href="index.html">Project</a> <a href="research.html">Learn</a> <a href="advisor_brief.html">Advisor Brief</a> <a href="project_status.html">Status</a> <a href="status.html">Live Status</a> <a href="roadmap.html">Roadmap</a> <a href="process.html">Process</a> <a href="record.html">Record</a> <a href="library.html" class="active">Sources</a> <a href="results.html">Measurements</a> </div> </nav> </header> <main> <div class="doc-layout"> <aside class="toc-sidebar"><div class="card-label">Table of contents</div><a href="#global-rules">Global Rules</a> <a href="#ladder">Ladder</a> <a href="#downgrade-examples">Downgrade Examples</a></aside> <div class="doc-wrap doc-source-docs-contracts-claims-ladder-md"> <p class="doc-meta"><a href="library.html">Back to sources</a> · rendered from <code>docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md</code></p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md · commit db150a0"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>contracts/<wbr>claims_ladder.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit db150a0</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Claims Ladder</h1> <p>Status: binding for reader-facing claims from Slice 2M onward. Decision D-037 records adoption. Per-claim IDs and mechanical enforcement arrive with the Phase 4 claims index; until then, authors apply this ladder during review.</p> <p>This contract governs wording in reports, slides, README/status prose, figure captions, and tables that a reader could treat as a result. Dated run reports, stream logs, council logs, and decision logs may preserve historical wording, but later reader-facing summaries must use the current level.</p> <p>The warning-only prose scan mechanically enumerates <code>README.md</code>, <code>PROJECT_STATUS.md</code>, <code>docs/report_src/**</code>, the generated Phase-4 claims projection, Markdown tables/captions under analysis and figure artifacts, and present or future <code>slides/</code>, <code>captions/</code>, and <code>tables/</code> publication trees. Historical <code>docs/run_reports/**</code> records and the decision/council/stream logs are deliberately outside that scan. Warning-only exit behavior remains the D-059 policy: these findings require editorial review but are not structural claim-gate failures.</p> <p>The canonical JSONL accepts two authority-distinct row dialects through one fail-closed validator: the single pre-P2-037 legacy L1 row only under its exact hash-pinned identity, and current rows linked to a governed <code>joulewise.claim_verdicts.v1</code> artifact. Rows with unknown authority fields or a mixture of legacy and engine-linked authority fields are invalid. Verdict semantics belong to <code>joulewise.analysis_engine</code>; the claims-index layer adds only linkage, canonical ordering/rendering, relative-path, editorial, and current production-admission checks. <code>two_look_alpha_spending</code> remains outside claims-index production admission until separately ruled in; current admission is deliberately <code>fixed_n</code> only.</p> <h2 id="global-rules">Global Rules</h2> <ul> <li>Strict validation is the entry ticket for evidence. A run bundle that cannot pass the applicable strict checks does not support a result claim.</li> <li>Measurement boundaries follow D-018. Claims must name the boundary label where it matters, for example <code>M3 Max / MLX / powermetrics SoC rails</code>, <code>RTX / vLLM / nvidia-smi board power</code>, or <code>wall_meter AC</code>.</li> <li>Cross-boundary comparisons are descriptive only unless a named calibration bundle exists for the compared boundaries. Calibration bundles include wall meter or USB-C PD evidence that explicitly bridges the boundary.</li> <li>Comparative claims from 2M use the experiment manifest order. Interleaved order is required where model reload and operational constraints permit; if block order is forced, the claim must say so and remain below L2 unless the Phase 4 drift audit clears it.</li> <li>Detection-floor gates follow Phase 4 Stage 4.0 and Stage 4.5. Effects below the floor are reported as <code>not resolvable</code>, not as wins, losses, or no difference.</li> <li>Energy-per-output-token claims require runtime-observed output token counts, the runtime stop reason, and the output policy label. If the denominator comes from config fallback rather than runtime observation, the claim downgrades to L0 capability language.</li> <li>(2026-07-09) Token-denominated metrics and cross-tokenizer comparison language follow <code>docs/contracts/token_normalization.md</code>, including its stack-identity table, across all surfaces this ladder governs.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ladder">Ladder</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Level</th> <th>Allowed Claim Shape</th> <th>Required Evidence</th> <th>Forbidden Language</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>L0 - Capability</td> <td>The harness can execute this path and preserve auditable evidence.</td> <td>One complete bundle; applicable strict validation; raw artifacts present; boundary label recorded. Config-fallback token denominators may appear only here.</td> <td>faster, cheaper, more efficient, scales, crossover, ranking, law, proves</td> </tr> <tr> <td>L1 - Instrument Result</td> <td>On this exact stack, boundary, workload, and output policy, this measured quantity was observed.</td> <td>n &gt;= 3 strict-valid bundles, or a single run only if explicitly labeled smoke/capability; runtime-observed token counts for per-token claims; stop reason and output policy label; no suspect quality flags unless waived in text.</td> <td>general device ranking, model-family law, cross-target winner, active-parameter scaling result</td> </tr> <tr> <td>L2 - Comparative Result</td> <td>Condition A differed from condition B within the same measurement boundary under a named workload and policy.</td> <td>n &gt;= 5 per condition; strict-valid bundles; 2M experiment manifest order recorded and interleaved where permitted; confidence intervals reported; effect clears the Phase 4 detection floor; same boundary label, or a named calibration bundle if boundaries differ.</td> <td>cross-boundary winner without calibration, universal, architecture-wide conclusion, extrapolated crossover</td> </tr> <tr> <td>L3 - Model Fit</td> <td>A fitted fixed/marginal model predicts held-out cells within stated error for the tested matrix.</td> <td>Designed matrix with holdout cells; strict-valid source bundles; runtime-observed token denominators; residual and sensitivity analysis; detection-floor audit for every fitted effect; boundaries and workload policies stated.</td> <td>law, universal scaling, architecture-wide result, causal language beyond the fitted variables</td> </tr> <tr> <td>L4 - Generalized Finding</td> <td>The finding holds across named stacks, units, or calibrated boundaries under stated limits.</td> <td>Independent replication across a second target or second unit; strict-valid bundles; n and order rules satisfied per condition; named calibration bundles for cross-boundary quantitative comparison; replicated runbook; sensitivity audit survives boundary and version changes.</td> <td>unqualified claims outside tested hardware, workloads, runtime versions, policies, or calibration scope</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <h2 id="downgrade-examples">Downgrade Examples</h2> <ul> <li>Two strict-valid Mac/MLX/powermetrics points that differ in model size, architecture, and quantization are hypothesis-generating for Q4. They are not an active-parameter scaling result.</li> <li>A same-boundary energy/token difference with runtime-observed token counts but fewer than five interleaved repetitions is L1 until the comparative protocol is satisfied.</li> <li>A per-token result using configured output length because runtime token counts were unavailable is L0 capability language, even if the bundle is otherwise strict-valid.</li> </ul> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/contracts/claims_ladder.md · commit db150a0 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
./docs/campaign_packs/c5_3_1_3_5_replication.md:28:| Unit of analysis + dependence structure | Bundle repetition within unit x workload cell, blocked by physical unit and session. Replication verdicts compare cell-level estimates, not individual telemetry samples. |
./docs/campaign_packs/c5_3_1_3_5_replication.md:29:| Estimator/formula | Estimate unit delta `delta_unit = metric(unit_b) - metric(unit_a)` and variance relative to the active P2-015 floor. Source-claim replication has exactly three outcomes: `replicated` (the original direction/verdict survives on the second unit under the frozen contrast rule), `contradicted` (the second-unit contrast is resolvable and reverses the original verdict), and `inconclusive` (the second-unit contrast is below floor or otherwise `not resolvable`). `inconclusive` is never reported as successful replication. A `practically equivalent` verdict is available only via a predeclared equivalence margin and equivalence test frozen in the registry before execution. |
./docs/campaign_packs/c5_3_1_3_5_replication.md:51:| Estimator/formula | Agreement check compares external-lab estimate to original estimate under the frozen tolerance: direction/verdict agreement plus absolute delta relative to active floor/MDE. Method-transfer success also requires strict validation and reproducible reduction from transferred artifacts. |

./docs/reviews/2026-07-08-technical-merit-review.md:52:1. **Q1 -- the split-energy crossover with joule-costed KV transfer.** Genuinely novel: two independent literature passes fail to find any published end-to-end energy measurement of PD-disaggregated inference across networked consumer devices with transfer costed in joules. Both verdicts are predeclared publishable, and transfer-time arithmetic places 1GbE in the crossover-possible regime. Its promise, stated precisely: *the first both-end-measured, per-stage (prefill/serialize/transfer/deserialize/decode) energy decomposition of disaggregated inference on consumer interconnects, with the crossover prompt length -- where splitting beats monolithic -- either located or excluded within the tested range.* The honest degradations: heterogeneous *measured* (not modeled) answers hang on the pending cross-backend KV-replay verdict; "transfer joules" are boundary-qualified; per-request transfer energies at realistic sizes will be regression-derived from a payload ladder, not directly resolved.
./docs/reviews/2026-07-08-technical-merit-review.md:58:Honestly routine: **Q5** (rank stability is standard benchmark-robustness work; the MDE-gated "unresolved tie" discipline is the contribution, not the answer), **Q3** (an analysis product of Q1/Q2's dataset, though at consumer links *both* the energy and latency axes of PD disaggregation are uncharacterized -- the correct charge is "no independent experiment," not "latency already done"), and the **affine-ladder energy-per-correct headline**, which is near-mechanical conditional on its envelope gate and on level-invariant per-item energy -- both empirical premises -- rather than scientifically central. The AP-5 C5-1.9 MoE-vs-dense energy-per-correct question is not tautological and should not be collapsed into that verdict. The scientifically interesting endpoint -- level-dependent per-item energy at fixed envelope -- is already the analysis plan's primary but should be the stated hypothesis. The measured 122B-vs-1.5B contrast carries essentially zero standalone weight (four-way confounded, n=3), and the project formally demoted it itself.

./docs/campaign_packs/split_suite_q1_q2_q3.md:36:| Metric + exact window class | Primary (single frozen estimand): `split_total_energy_j = prefill + serialize + transfer + deserialize + decode` as composite GROSS request energy, under the frozen service-state assumption of two already-powered warm nodes (decode-node model loaded before the measured window); the headline crossover verdict uses this basis only. Named sensitivity analyses, never headline-eligible: `SENS-SPLIT-Q1-IDLESUB` (composite idle-subtracted request energy, with each end's own idle floor subtracted over its own stage windows, computed only where both ends have usable idle baselines; consistent with D-067, reader-facing reporting is limited to clearly labeled per-end, within-device marginal diagnostics and cannot support a split-vs-monolithic contrast, configuration rank, Pareto frontier, or crossover verdict) and `SENS-SPLIT-Q1-PROVISION` (gross composite plus the decode-oriented second node's measured idle power charged for the full request duration; descriptive, L1 ceiling). Stage descriptors use gross phase windows: `phase_energy_j.prefill`, `phase_energy_j.serialize`, `phase_energy_j.transfer`, `phase_energy_j.deserialize`, and `phase_energy_j.decode`. |
./docs/campaign_packs/split_suite_q1_q2_q3.md:38:| Estimator/formula | For each frozen cell, estimate two predeclared contrasts: `delta_prefill_ref_j = split_total_energy_j - monolithic_total_j(prefill_node)` and `delta_decode_ref_j = split_total_energy_j - monolithic_total_j(decode_node)`, each with paired/block contrast when the monolithic reruns are in the same campaign block, otherwise the predeclared unpaired contrast with session covariate. Both contrasts enter the enumerated FAM-SPLIT-Q1-ENERGY-CROSSOVER contrast_id set and are Holm-adjusted within the family. "Split wins" in a cell is an intersection–union verdict: it holds only if BOTH Holm-adjusted 95% contrast intervals lie entirely below zero AND both contrasts clear the active floor gate; if either contrast fails, the cell verdict is "no crossover" or `not resolvable` per the three-way wording rule (D-053). No comparator may be selected after observing the data; the observed-minimum reference is forbidden. D-048 prediction validation also estimates prediction error `measured_split_total_j - predicted_split_total_j` on the GROSS basis, where prediction is the prefill-node AP-1 gross-fit terms plus GROSS measured-or-predicted serialize energy plus measured link-transfer energy plus GROSS measured-or-predicted deserialize energy plus the decode-node AP-1 gross-fit terms before any split hardware run; each node's fixed/overhead contribution is that node's AP-1 GROSS-FITTED fixed term, never a measured idle-floor substitute or an additional idle-floor charge. Crossover exists only where the intersection–union verdict above holds (both references beaten under joint Holm-adjusted intervals, both clearing the floor gate). |

class="doc-meta"><a href="library.html">Back to sources</a> · rendered from <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code></p> <div class="provenance-plate"><span class="source-chip" title="TASK_QUEUE.md · commit de665ea"><span class="source-file">TASK_QUEUE.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit de665ea</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>JouleWise Task Queue</h1> <p>This is the live queue for JouleWise work. When the user gives a new task, first triage it here instead of assuming it should happen immediately.</p> <h2 id="intake-rule-for-new-tasks">Intake Rule For New Tasks</h2> <p>For every new user task:</p> <ol> <li>Read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</li> <li>Read this file.</li> <li>Check <code>git status --short --branch</code>.</li> <li>Review the last 2-3 commits with <code>git log --oneline --decorate -3</code>.</li> <li>Check relevant handoffs in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>.</li> <li>If <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> contains an ACTIVE <code>ACTIVE_STOP_CARD</code>, that card outranks this queue. Execute or preserve the card&#39;s resume/cleanup instructions before considering any lower-ranked work.</li> <li>Decide whether the task is:<ul> <li>urgent workspace hygiene,</li> <li>Phase 1 evidence work,</li> <li>Phase 2 implementation prep,</li> <li>later-phase research work,</li> <li>documentation/reporting,</li> <li>or unrelated/new scope.</li> </ul> </li> <li>Place or update the task in the queue with priority, rationale, evidence, and blockers.</li> <li>If executing it now, say why it outranks the current top task.</li> <li>Closure rule (D-023): a row may move to Completed only after the corresponding phase exit-checklist matrix row already shows the same status with dated evidence, and the Completed row&#39;s evidence cell must cite that matrix row (file + item id). If no matrix row exists for the work, say so explicitly in the evidence cell.</li> </ol> <h2 id="priority-scale">Priority Scale</h2> <ul> <li><strong>P0 Safety</strong>: prevents accidental data loss, bad commits, broken handoffs, or corrupted repo state.</li> <li><strong>P1 Phase Gate</strong>: required to close the current phase or unblock the next phase responsibly.</li> <li><strong>P2 Next Slice</strong>: next implementation slice after current phase gates are adequately planned or closed.</li> <li><strong>P3 Research Expansion</strong>: useful experiment or feature, but not needed for current gate.</li> <li><strong>P4 Polish</strong>: quality-of-life, dashboard polish, formatting, cleanup, or presentation work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ranking-factors">Ranking Factors</h2> <p>Rank higher when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Prevents accidental loss or bad Git history.</li> <li>Produces evidence for the current phase exit checklist.</li> <li>Removes ambiguity for multiple later steps.</li> <li>Is required before physical hardware time is spent.</li> <li>Is cheap to verify and reduces future confusion.</li> <li>Matches the current phase better than jumping ahead.</li> </ul> <p>Rank lower when a task:</p> <ul> <li>Depends on unavailable hardware or supervisor input.</li> <li>Is a later-phase feature.</li> <li>Adds polish before a runnable vertical slice exists.</li> <li>Produces code without a clear run-bundle or test artifact.</li> </ul> <h2 id="ready-shelf-rule">Ready/Shelf Rule</h2> <p>A partially built or proposed task is <strong>READY</strong> only when it has:</p> <ul> <li>one authority document or stream-log pointer,</li> <li>bounded files/modules or a bounded artifact target,</li> <li>explicit acceptance evidence or a verification command,</li> <li>no hidden hardware/user/token-budget dependency, and</li> <li>a named lane (<code>[AGENT]</code>, <code>[QUIET-MAC]</code>, or <code>[ED-EXTERNAL]</code>).</li> </ul> <p>If any of those are missing, keep the item as a shelved concept or planning note instead of letting it compete with executable queue work. Half-finished work should be resumed only through its authority pointer and stop-card/checkpoint state, not by inference from prose summaries.</p> <h2 id="machine-state-lanes-adopted-c-007-2026-07-07">Machine-State Lanes (adopted C-007, 2026-07-07)</h2> <p>Every task carries a lane; a session picks the top task COMPATIBLE with its machine state, not the top task absolutely:</p> <ul> <li><strong>[QUIET-MAC]</strong> — measurement campaigns only: no agent fleet, no Codex load, idle gate will flag contamination.</li> <li><strong>[AGENT]</strong> — code, docs, feasibility spikes; safe during agent-heavy sessions.</li> <li><strong>[ED-EXTERNAL]</strong> — needs the user: advisor, calendar, device access, purchases, destinations.</li> </ul> <h2 id="historical-queue-snapshot-superseded-2026-07-15">Historical Queue Snapshot (superseded 2026-07-15)</h2> <p>The former hand-authored live table was removed because it duplicated kernel tasks. If dates compress, protect Phase 2&#39;s Mac slice and Phase 3&#39;s synthetic sweep first (the R-012 floor), and shrink Phase 3&#39;s matrix before shrinking Phase 4&#39;s audit rigor.</li> <li>Slides (5.4) want frozen figures &gt;=1 week before the colloquium; the report (5.5) wants the claims-index final pass &gt;=1 week before submission. Work backwards from there when dates land.</li> <li>Heartbeat (added 2026-07-05): if more than 14 days pass with no run report and no recorded break in this file, the next session starts with a milestones + risk-register review before any other work - a calendar-risk-dominated project must notice its own silence. <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Agent Implementation Plan</h1> <p>This repository implements JouleWise, an extensible energy-characterization benchmark for LLM inference across heterogeneous local hardware. The name is a nod to JouleSort and Splitwise: energy measurement as the spine, split inference as the first research application that validates the harness.</p> <h2 id="ground-rules-for-agents">Ground Rules For Agents</h2> <ul> <li>At the start of every substantial run, read <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> first.</li> <li>For any new/random user task, triage it in <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code> before deciding whether it outranks the current phase work.</li> <li>At the start of each phase or major step, apply <code>docs/planning_reflection_protocol.md</code> before implementation.</li> <li>At the end of every substantial run, update <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> and add or update a detailed report in <code>docs/run_reports/</code>. If advisor-visible state changed (a phase or gate closed, a verdict landed, the schedule moved), refresh <code>PROJECT_STATUS.md</code> too.</li> <li>Check <code>docs/decision_log.md</code> before re-deciding anything; record new design decisions there with options and considerations.</li> <li>Per-item phase status is asserted only in <code>docs/phase_N/phase_N_exit_checklist.md</code> (D-023); this file&#39;s checkboxes are a coarse mirror updated at slice/phase closes.</li> <li>Review <code>docs/risk_register.md</code> at phase starts and when a trigger fires.</li> <li>Keep run artifacts self-contained and reproducible.</li> <li>Prefer small vertical slices that produce complete run bundles.</li> <li>Treat unsupported hardware/model combinations as structured outcomes, not crashes.</li> <li>Keep runtime adapters separate from telemetry adapters.</li> <li>Make every result traceable to a config, raw power trace, event log, and reducer output.</li> </ul> <h2 id="single-source-of-truth-map">Single Source Of Truth Map</h2> <p>Detail lives in exactly one place; everything else links to it. When documents disagree, fix the drift in the same run and note it in the run report.</p> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>Artifact</th> <th>Owns</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td><code>AGENT_PLAN.md</code> (this file)</td> <td>phase index, coarse status mirror, acceptance criteria (per-item status authority: the exit checklists, D-023)</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>PROJECT_STATUS.md</code></td> <td>advisor-facing status/plan/architecture summary (derived; update when advisor-visible state changes)</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/phase_N/phase_N_plan.md</code></td> <td>step/slice detail: objectives, design, actions, evidence, fallbacks</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/phase_N/phase_N_exit_checklist.md</code></td> <td>evidence gates for closing phase N, and per-item status (the authority, D-023)</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code></td> <td>what to do next, and why it outranks the rest</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/agent_playbook.md</code></td> <td>per-mission execution guides for agents: read-first lists, code-level routes, verification, handoff checklists</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>RUN_STATE.md</code></td> <td>current handoff: state, verification, next step</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/decision_log.md</code></td> <td>design decisions, options, considerations</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/risk_register.md</code></td> <td>risks, triggers, mitigations, descope ladder</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/milestones.md</code></td> <td>calendar constraints and phase target dates</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/contracts/measurement_methodology.md</code></td> <td>measurement rules (boundaries, clocks, statistics)</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/contracts/run_bundle_layout.md</code></td> <td>bundle artifact contract</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/contracts/adapter_contracts.md</code></td> <td>adapter behavior contracts</td> </tr> <tr> <td><code>docs/contracts/node_worker_protocol.md</code></td> <td>remote-execution protocol (transport-independent; pinned during 2K, reused by 2L + Phase 3)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <p>Superseded (2026-07-15, WO-021; D-043): <code>docs/process/state_kernel.json</code> is the sole editable authority for live work selection, while generated <code>TASK_QUEUE.md</code> and <code>RUN_STATE.md</code> regions are projections; · commit dbd8137"><span class="source-file">docs/<wbr>risk_register.md</span><span class="source-commit">commit dbd8137</span></span></div> <!-- rendered: marked@18.0.6 --> <h1>Risk Register</h1> <p>Living register of risks that could sink, delay, or weaken the capstone. Review at the start of every phase and whenever a trigger fires; update statuses at the end of substantial runs alongside <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>.</p> <p>Conventions:</p> <ul> <li>Likelihood/Impact: low / medium / high, judged against the current phase.</li> <li>Trigger: the observable event that means the risk is materializing.</li> <li>Mitigation: what we do <em>now</em> to reduce likelihood or impact.</li> <li>Fallback: what we do <em>if it happens</em> - every fallback must preserve a publishable result, even if smaller.</li> <li>Owner: <code>user</code> for actions needing human/lab/supervisor access, <code>agent</code> for repo work.</li> </ul> <h2 id="summary">Summary</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Risk</th> <th>Phase</th> <th>Likelihood</th> <th>Impact</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>R-001</td> <td>Supervisor approval delayed or scope shifts</td> <td>1</td> <td>medium</td> <td>high</td> <td>all</td> <td>medium</td> <td>high</td> <td>mitigated-in-policy (D-060 RATIFIED 2026-07-10; enforcement = queue discipline + spend guardrails, WO-022/R2, <code>docs/orchestration.md</code> §Spend guardrails)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <h2 id="r-001-supervisor-approval-delayed-or-scope-shifts">R-001: Supervisor approval delayed or scope shifts</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 1. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high (wrong deliverable built).</li> <li>Trigger: Phase 2 implementation slices ready to start (2A-2F complete) with P1-001 still open; or any supervisor communication contradicting <code>AGENT_PLAN.md</code> scope.</li> <li>Status note (2026-07-05): the first trigger fired 2026-06-12 (2A-2F completed with P1-001 still open). The mitigation is holding as designed - all work since has been hardware-independent and harness-shaped (mock slice, docs, Slice 2N is next and is also ungated) - and the fallback (&quot;continue only mock/local work; hardware purchases/borrows blocked-on-approval&quot;) is effectively in force.</li> <li>Mitigation: the queue keeps P1-001 ranked first; all work until approval stays hardware-independent and harness-shaped (valuable under any scope); the Phase 1 exit checklist lists the exact questions to put to the supervisor so one meeting can close the gate.</li> <li>Fallback: if approval stalls past mock-slice completion, continue only mock/local work and mark every hardware purchase or borrow decision blocked-on-approval.</li> <li>Owner: user.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-002-powermetrics-sudo-workflow-not-approved-on-measurement-mac">R-002: powermetrics sudo workflow not approved on measurement Mac</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: low (user controls the machine; a local auth session needs rescheduling - the planned 2026-06-10 slot passed without one). Impact: high (no Mac telemetry = no flagship vertical slice).</li> <li>Status: closed-residual (2026-07-08). The working Mac slice completed 2G/2H/2I on 2026-07-06 with privileged powermetrics capture and strict-valid bundles; revisit for new macOS/MLX/powermetrics versions or new Mac hardware.</li> <li>Trigger: scoped sudoers rule (D-004) cannot be installed, or privileged sample capture fails after the auth session.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-004 defines a minimal, single-binary sudoers rule with the exact line documented in the Phase 1 exit checklist&#39;s instrumentation section; interactive-sudo manual fallback documented for attended runs.</li> <li>Fallback: attended runs with interactive sudo (operator present per experiment); if even that is unacceptable, the Mac becomes runtime-supported/telemetry-blocked and the first real slice moves to the first available CUDA target - recorded as a finding, not hidden.</li> <li>Owner: user (install rule), agent (pre-check + structured failure).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-003-mlx-install-or-model-load-failure-on-mac">R-003: MLX install or model-load failure on Mac</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: low. Impact: medium (delays flagship slice).</li> <li>Status: closed-residual (2026-07-08). The working Mac slice completed 2G/2H/2I on 2026-07-06 with MLX generation and strict-valid bundles; revisit for new MLX/mlx-lm versions or new Mac hardware.</li> <li>Trigger: <code>pip install mlx mlx-lm</code> fails, or the chosen model (D-016) has no working MLX artifact.</li> <li>Mitigation: install into a dedicated venv with versions recorded in run bundles; model criteria (D-016) require known MLX availability before selection; smoke-test load before scheduling measurement sessions.</li> <li>Fallback: llama.cpp with the Metal backend as the Mac runtime (already a planned runtime for split portability under D-015); the MLX adapter then becomes optional rather than flagship.</li> <li>Owner: agent (with user approving installs).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-004-kv-persist-resume-unsupported-in-a-target-runtime">R-004: KV persist/resume unsupported in a target runtime</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium overall (high for vLLM file-based replay, low for llama.cpp, low-medium for mlx-lm). Impact: high if unmitigated - this is the project&#39;s central feasibility risk.</li> <li>Trigger: a Stage 3.0 spike returns <code>replay_unsupported</code> for a runtime needed by a planned pairing.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-015&#39;s feasibility ladder - spikes run <em>before</em> any split hardware time is scheduled; pairings are planned only on runtimes with <code>replay_supported</code> verdicts; the synthetic transfer microbenchmark (Stage 3.1) is independent of all runtime cooperation and guarantees a crossover dataset.</li> <li>Fallback: analytical composition - measured prefill energy (node A) + measured synthetic transfer energy (payload sized by the KV model) + measured decode energy (node B) bounds the split cost honestly; the report states the composition method explicitly.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-005-llama-cpp-cache-files-not-portable-across-machines-backends">R-005: llama.cpp cache files not portable across machines/backends</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium (session files are version- and model-sensitive; cross-backend CUDA-save -&gt; Metal-load is unverified). Impact: high for <em>heterogeneous</em> pairings specifically.</li> <li>Trigger: Stage 3.0.2&#39;s cross-machine restore test fails or produces divergent output.</li> <li>Mitigation: the spike tests cross-machine restore explicitly, with pinned identical llama.cpp versions and identical GGUF files on both ends, before any heterogeneous experiment is scheduled.</li> <li>Fallback: restrict offline-replay pairings to same-platform pairs (GPU-&gt;GPU in the borrow window, Orin-&gt;Orin); cover heterogeneous pairs with the analytical composition (R-004 fallback); report the portability finding itself - it is a legitimate disaggregation-practicality result.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-006-3080-ti-borrow-window-slips-or-shrinks">R-006: 3080 Ti borrow window slips or shrinks</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium (loses GPU-&gt;GPU pairing, not the phase).</li> <li>Trigger: window not scheduled by Phase 3 Stage 3.2 completion; or window arrives before split tooling is ready.</li> <li>Mitigation: all split tooling reaches rehearsed-on-available-hardware state before the window (the Phase 3 plan keeps a borrow-window runbook so borrow time is execution-only, no debugging); calendar mapping task (P1-008) makes the window a tracked date.</li> <li>Fallback: GPU-&gt;GPU pairing drops to single-GPU prefill/decode phase decomposition plus analytical composition; 3050&lt;-&gt;Orin and Orin&lt;-&gt;Orin remain.</li> <li>Owner: user (scheduling), agent (runbook readiness).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-007-no-wall-meter-available">R-007: No wall meter available</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 1-4. Likelihood: medium. Impact: medium (boundary calibration and Pi/Hailo coverage lost; per-target results stand).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-003 resolves &quot;unavailable&quot;.</li> <li>Mitigation: P1-003 is a Phase 1 gate precisely so this resolves before it matters; D-018&#39;s boundary table makes results honest without a meter.</li> <li>Fallback: report within-target comparisons (always boundary-consistent) as primary; flag cross-target absolute comparisons with the boundary caveat; targets with no platform telemetry (Pi) become telemetry-unavailable findings.</li> <li>Owner: user.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-008-orin-telemetry-inaccessible">R-008: Orin telemetry inaccessible</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-3. Likelihood: medium (rail sysfs paths vary by L4T version). Impact: low (one target of several).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-006 evidence shows neither INA3221 sysfs nor tegrastats usable.</li> <li>Mitigation: two candidate mechanisms documented before hardware time; wall-meter fallback if R-007 resolves positively.</li> <li>Fallback: Orin runs runtime-only (latency/throughput) marked telemetry-unavailable, or drops to a stretch target.</li> <li>Owner: user (access), agent (adapter).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-009-hailo-cannot-run-llm-shaped-workloads">R-009: Hailo cannot run LLM-shaped workloads</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 1. Likelihood: high. Impact: low - <em>by design</em>: the plan treats Hailo as a feasibility investigation whose negative verdict is itself a reportable applicability finding.</li> <li>Status: <strong>realized as expected, 2026-06-12</strong> — verdict <code>unsupported_workload</code>. The trigger fired (a non-<code>supported</code> verdict), the by-design mitigation held, and the outcome is the publishable applicability finding the plan anticipated. No schedule impact.</li> <li>Trigger: feasibility checklist closes with any non-<code>supported</code> verdict. (Fired 2026-06-12.)</li> <li>Mitigation: none needed; the verdict-code structure in the Phase 1 exit checklist&#39;s Hailo section makes the outcome publishable either way. Do not spend implementation effort on a Hailo backend (the verdict is now recorded; the standing do-not-do-yet rule becomes &quot;report, don&#39;t implement&quot;).</li> <li>Fallback: Pi 5 CPU-only llama.cpp with wall-meter telemetry becomes an optional low-power data point if the meter exists; otherwise Pi/Hailo appears only in the applicability table.</li> <li>Owner: user (device access), agent (verdict documentation - done).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-010-controller-as-dut-contamination-on-mac-runs">R-010: Controller-as-DUT contamination on Mac runs</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2. Likelihood: high if unmitigated. Impact: medium (biased flagship numbers).</li> <li>Status: mitigated by D-013 (idle baseline includes resident quiescent controller; deferred logging; blocking wait during measured window).</li> <li>Trigger (residual): SSH-controlled comparison runs (once transport exists) show a delta beyond run-to-run variance.</li> <li>Fallback: move Mac headline measurements to remote-controlled runs.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-011-benchmark-network-cannot-be-isolated">R-011: Benchmark network cannot be isolated</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 3. Likelihood: medium (campus/home network constraints unknown until P1-004 closes). Impact: medium (noisy transfer measurements).</li> <li>Trigger: P1-004 topology answer shows shared links only.</li> <li>Mitigation: prefer direct node-to-node cabling (no switch) for 1GbE/2.5GbE point-to-point tests - removes the isolation question entirely for two-node experiments; record link conditions per run in the bundle.</li> <li>Fallback: run sweeps off-hours, repeat n&gt;=5, report observed throughput alongside nominal link speed (the bundle already records measured throughput per D-008&#39;s transfer block).</li> <li>Owner: user (hardware), agent (recording).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-012-schedule-five-phases-vs-fixed-academic-deadlines">R-012: Schedule: five phases vs fixed academic deadlines</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high (capstones fail by calendar, not by code).</li> <li>Trigger: any phase exceeding its (to-be-set) calendar budget; colloquium or report dates announced (P1-008) leaving less runway than the plan assumes.</li> <li>Mitigation: P1-008 maps phases to real dates as soon as the user supplies them (<code>docs/milestones.md</code> holds the skeleton); every phase defines a hardware-independent floor and a descope ladder so cutting is a decision, not a scramble.</li> <li>Descope ladder (worst-case minimum viable capstone, in cut order):<ol> <li>Drop live split (3.3) - already stretch.</li> <li>Drop 10GbE and one model size.</li> <li>Drop heterogeneous replay pairs (keep synthetic transfer + analytical composition).</li> <li>Drop Orin/Pi targets (keep Mac + one CUDA).</li> <li>Floor: mock harness + Mac vertical slice + homogeneous baselines + synthetic interconnect sweep + analytical split model. This is still a complete, defensible benchmark-plus-study.</li> </ol> </li> <li>Owner: user (dates), agent (floor discipline).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-013-thermal-throttling-confounds-measurements">R-013: Thermal throttling confounds measurements</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-4. Likelihood: medium (high on passively-cooled Orin/Pi). Impact: medium (rep-to-rep drift, biased late reps).</li> <li>Status: mitigated by D-014 (idle-power recovery gate between reps, thermal_drift_c in measurement quality, interleaved ordering) - residual risk on targets without thermal sensors.</li> <li>Trigger: thermal_drift_c trending across reps, or cooldown cap hits recorded in bundles.</li> <li>Fallback: longer cooldowns, active cooling notes recorded in run metadata, or excluding throttled reps <em>with documented cause</em> per D-014.</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-014-model-weights-become-unavailable-or-gated">R-014: Model weights become unavailable or gated</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2+. Likelihood: low. Impact: medium (mid-project model swap breaks comparability).</li> <li>Trigger: chosen model&#39;s hub entry gated/removed; license terms change.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-016 requires mirroring chosen weights to local storage immediately on selection, with revisions and hashes recorded.</li> <li>Fallback: promote the recorded fallback candidate; re-run affected baselines (the config hash separates old/new data cleanly).</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-015-schema-changes-after-data-collection-starts">R-015: Schema changes after data collection starts</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2+. Likelihood: low. Impact: high (existing bundles unreadable or silently misread).</li> <li>Status: mitigated structurally.</li> <li>Mitigation: schema_version field exists from v0.1; D-008 plans the only anticipated breaking-shape change (v0.2) <em>before</em> split data collection; output-schema additions are additive-only (the JSON schema does not forbid additional properties); <code>validate-bundle</code> pins what a valid bundle means per version.</li> <li>Trigger: any proposed non-additive change to a schema with bundles already on disk.</li> <li>Fallback: a dated migration note in this repo plus a one-shot migration script; never edit bundles in place (they are evidence).</li> <li>Owner: agent.</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-016-measurement-corpus-loss-runs-has-no-backup-path">R-016: Measurement-corpus loss (runs/ has no backup path)</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: 2-5. Likelihood: low. Impact: high (the dataset behind every claim is a gitignored directory on one disk; a disk failure or an errant delete erases the evidence the defense rests on, and hardware re-collection needs access windows that may not recur).</li> <li>Trigger: first real (non-mock) bundle written; any data-affecting incident (disk error, iCloud eviction anomaly, accidental delete).</li> <li>Mitigation: before the first real measurement session (gate on 2I data collection, tracked as queue task P0-002), define and record the backup protocol here: destination (external disk and/or cloud location outside the repo), cadence (after every measurement session), method (rsync of <code>runs/</code> plus experiment manifests), and a restore test performed once. Configs + manifests already make re-collection well-defined; backups make it unnecessary.</li> <li><strong>Protocol recorded (2026-07-06, P0-002 closed interim).</strong> Destination: <code>~/JouleWise-backup</code> — a user-directed INTERIM location on the same disk (&quot;cursory... I&#39;ll handle that later&quot;); it protects against errant deletes but not disk failure, so the user still owes an external/cloud destination for full mitigation. Cadence: after every measurement session. Method: <code>scripts/backup_runs.sh [RUNS_DIR] [DEST]</code> (rsync -a, never <code>--delete</code>; dated UTC log line per invocation appended to <code>DEST/backup.log</code>). Restore test performed 2026-07-06: mock bundle backed up, restored to a temp dir, <code>validate-bundle</code> green on the restored copy. Swapping in the final destination is a one-argument change (or edit the script default) plus one fresh restore test.</li> <li><strong>Protocol upgraded (2026-07-10/11, P0-003 closed; addendum 2026-07-16 closing a summary-row/body drift found by the resumption audit).</strong> The interim same-disk destination above is superseded: the external destination is iCloud Drive, live with a fresh backup + restore test passed (evidence: <code>docs/run_reports/2026-07-11-c028-continuation.md</code> §11, &quot;The P0-003 iCloud measurement-corpus backup and restore gate is satisfied&quot;). The 2026-07-06 entry above is retained as history. Standing caveat: iCloud eviction — re-verify the destination is materialized (fresh restore test) before each measurement window.</li> <li>Fallback: re-run affected experiments from their configs (the config hash separates old/new data cleanly per D-005/D-010); report any unrecoverable gap honestly in the exclusion log.</li> <li>Owner: user (destination/media), agent (protocol doc + restore test).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-017-repo-lives-on-icloud-synced-desktop-eperm-lock-recurrence">R-017: Repo lives on iCloud-synced Desktop (EPERM lock recurrence)</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: low (mitigated; was high while on Desktop). Impact: medium (blocks work sessions mid-run; small integrity risk around eviction during writes).</li> <li>Status: <strong>mitigated 2026-07-05</strong> - the repo moved off the synced Desktop (current canonical path: <code>~/code/JouleWise</code>; the interim <code>~/code/CapstoneRivoire/Capstone</code> path recorded here was itself later renamed - corrected 2026-07-09, C-027). P0-001 complete; git + suite verified green at the new path. Residual exposure: agent sessions launched from the stale Desktop path (delete the leftover <code>~/Desktop/CapstoneRivoire</code> husk after relaunching from the new path), and any future placement of repo or <code>runs/</code> data under an iCloud-synced directory - do not.</li> <li>Trigger: any <code>Operation not permitted</code> on read/readdir inside the repo with the iCloud file provider (<code>bird</code>) active.</li> <li>History: first incident 2026-06-12 (documented in <code>RUN_STATE.md</code>); recurred 2026-07-05 mid-run - <code>docs/</code>, <code>joulewise/</code>, <code>tests/</code>, <code>.git</code>, and the repo root EPERM-locked intermittently during an active iCloud full-sync, clearing and re-locking per subtree. Both incidents match iCloud &quot;Optimize Mac Storage&quot; behavior on <code>~/Desktop/</code>. The move landed the same day as the second incident.</li> <li>Fallback: if a lock ever strikes again, wait for it to clear (both incidents did), then re-verify with the test suite before continuing; the remote (<code>origin/main</code>) bounds code loss to the working tree.</li> <li>Owner: user (launch paths), agent (post-lock verification discipline).</li> </ul> <h2 id="r-018-the-agent-loop-itself-as-a-schedule-and-scope-risk">R-018: The agent loop itself as a schedule and scope risk</h2> <ul> <li>Phase: all. Likelihood: medium. Impact: high (capstones fail by calendar, R-012).</li> <li>Registered by C-027 (NEGSPACE lens finding accepted in council): the multi-agent workflow can remain locally productive - packs, registries, meta-process, site work - while the graded deliverable path (rubric, report source, backup, real corpus, figures) stays starved. Same-day evidence at registration: ~6M tokens of breadth work vs six real corpus bundles, no report source, same-disk backup.</li> <li>Trigger: an agent-heavy work block that produces neither a new real evidence bundle nor a report/figure increment.</li> <li>Mitigation: D-060 depth-before-breadth stop line (RATIFIED by Ed 2026-07-10) extended by the WO-022/R2 spend guardrails (<code>docs/orchestration.md</code> §Spend guardrails, 2026-07-15); RPT-001 vertical slice; the C-027 correctness rows ranked ahead of all breadth work.</li> <li>Owner: lead (queue discipline + guardrail checkpoints), Ed (HARD bands and structure).</li> </ul> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/risk_register.md · commit dbd8137 · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>

Log</h1> <p>This is the canonical record of design decisions for JouleWise. Every decision that binds later work, trades off real alternatives, or would otherwise need to be re-derived by a future agent gets an entry here.</p> <h2 id="how-to-use-this-log">How To Use This Log</h2> <ul> <li>Before implementing anything non-trivial, check whether a decision here already covers it. Do not silently re-decide settled questions.</li> <li>When you make a new decision of this kind during a run, add an entry, link it from the run report, and reference its ID (<code>D-NNN</code>) in the code review or doc that applies it.</li> <li>Statuses: <code>accepted</code> (binding until revisited), <code>open</code> (criteria defined, evidence pending), <code>proposed</code> (recorded, awaiting Ed&#39;s ratification), <code>superseded by D-NNN</code>.</li> <li>Every entry must include Options Considered and Considerations. A decision without recorded alternatives is not auditable.</li> <li>Revisit triggers are part of the contract: when a trigger fires, the decision must be re-examined, not quietly worked around.</li> </ul> <h2 id="index">Index</h2> <div class="table-scroll"><table> <thead> <tr> <th>ID</th> <th>Title</th> <th>Status</th> </tr> </thead> <tbody><tr> <td>D-001</td> <td>Run bundles store normalized <code>config.json</code>, not YAML</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-002</td> <td>Telemetry sampling via subprocess + file, no controller threading</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-003</td> <td>Timestamp and clock-alignment policy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-004</td> <td><code>powermetrics</code> privilege workflow</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-005</td> <td>One bundle per repetition, grouped by experiment manifest</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-006</td> <td>Dashboard v1 is a static HTML report generator</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-007</td> <td>YAML config input is deferred</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-008</td> <td>Split runs arrive via schema v0.2 (<code>run_kind</code> + <code>split_plan</code>)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-009</td> <td>Dependency policy: stdlib core, optional extras</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-010</td> <td>Run ID scheme</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-011</td> <td><code>summary_metrics.json</code> is the bundle completion marker</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-012</td> <td>Failure-reason to run-status mapping</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-013</td> <td>Controller-as-DUT mitigation for Mac-local runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-014</td> <td>Statistical protocol for repeated runs</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-015</td> <td>Split-mechanism priority and same-runtime rule</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-016</td> <td>Benchmark model selection</td> <td>open (provisional small-model pick 2026-07-06; idle-subtracted is a labeled within-device secondary view</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-068</td> <td>Site deployment is Ed-manual; sessions end with a drift report, never a deploy</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-069</td> <td>Advisor-doc alignment (stream S-0) is sanctioned front-facing work</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-070</td> <td>Architectural-axes extension agenda (AXI): scope, claim posture, batch-axis rulings</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-071</td> <td>G10 memory-fit rule ratified (axi-sd-memory-fit-shape-v1); device-list review opened</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td>D-072</td> <td>Standing self-merge-with-full-gate authority (gh merges included)</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-073">D-073</a></td> <td>D-016 device-list amendment: Mac + 3080 Ti primary fleet, 12 GiB cap</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-074">D-074</a></td> <td>Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-075">D-075</a></td> <td>Extension-axis intake: ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-076">D-076</a></td> <td>Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review): measured-first budgets</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log_archive_1.html#d-077">D-077</a></td> <td>Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</td> <td>accepted</td> </tr> <tr> <td><a href="decision_log.html#d-078">D-078</a></td> <td>Soundness gate: no claim-bearing extraction from time-anchor-defective powermetrics corpora</td> <td>accepted; operative under Ed&#39;s direction through the full repair arc (close-out cap explicitly Ed-ratified 2026-07-22; original-text ratification rides PR #79 review)</td> </tr> </tbody></table></div> <hr> <blockquote> <p><strong>Site view:</strong> the complete entry index appears above; the 72 older full entries are omitted from this page for capsule size. The complete log is the repository file <a href="https://github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise/blob/main/docs/decision_log.md"><code>docs/decision_log.md</code></a>.</p> </blockquote> <span id="d-073"></span><h2 id="d-073-d-016-device-list-amendment-mac-3080-ti-primary-fleet-12-gib-cap">D-073: D-016 device-list amendment — Mac + 3080 Ti primary fleet, 12 GiB cap</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the D-071 brief, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/brief.md</code>). The primary cross-target fleet is the 128 GB M3 Max Mac and the 3080 Ti (12 GiB) rig; the G10 capacity cap re-floors from 8 GiB to <strong>12 GiB</strong> (3080 Ti class sets the floor). Jetson hardware is retained as OPTIONAL, non-cap-setting replication — the edge/8 GiB cell can be added later as a replication row without re-deciding this. The split study&#39;s two nodes are the Mac and the 3080 Ti rig. Big models remain open via the Mac-only subsystem (D-071 clause 3). Follow-ons ruled by Ed same session: (a) conditional primary-model repin remains open with a WIDENED candidate search under the new cap (Ed: &quot;is there really nothing better than Qwen3-1.7B? Gemma 4B or something?&quot;) — 3-4B-class models now fit comfortably; (b) dense/MoE pair re-search under the 12 GiB cap (OLMo dense arm failed G4 as published — see the OLMo verification record in the same trace directory).</p> <span id="d-074"></span><h2 id="d-074-conditional-qwen3-4b-primary-repin-olmo-1b-conversion-spike-authorized">D-074: Conditional Qwen3-4B primary repin + OLMo-1B conversion spike authorized</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-16. Owner: Ed (ruled on the 12 GiB model search, <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-16-device-list-brief/model-search-12gib.md</code>). (1) Qwen3-4B becomes the D-016 primary CONDITIONALLY: the repin lands only when the evidence gates pass (immutable source/license, MLX-Q4/GGUF-Q4/CUDA artifact receipts, three-runtime generation, G10 at the 12 GiB cap, KV receipts, thinking-mode policy pinned); any gate failure retains Qwen2.5-1.5B. New evidence era on success: manifests + quant ladder regenerate from one frozen source revision; Qwen2.5 results preserved as legacy. Runner-up Qwen3-1.7B; Gemma-3-4B rejected for the gated custom license + multimodal MLX seam. (2) The time-boxed OLMo-1B original-format→MLX conversion spike is authorized; success revives the matched OLMoE pair, failure files the dated negative finding and the pair defers (Option C) without re-litigation. Both execute next session as agent-lane work.</p> <span id="d-075"></span><h2 id="d-075-extension-axis-intake-ranked-fold-in-without-new-thesis-proliferation">D-075: Extension-axis intake — ranked fold-in without new thesis proliferation</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted (Ed-directed intake via the 2026-07-17 evaluation)</li> <li>Phase: Phase 2+ research program</li> </ul> <p>Context: Ed directed a six-axis evaluation and ratified the resulting roadmap at <code>docs/process_traces/2026-07-17-extension-axes/roadmap-synthesis.md</code>. D-055 keeps C5 deliberation in the bank and the registry as the canonical live index; D-070 keeps these axes as stress tests of Q4, caps candidate commitments at L2, and reserves commitment authority to Ed. The disposition ledger is <code>docs/stream_logs/2026-07-17-axes-foldin.md</code>.</p> <p>Decision:</p> <ol> <li>Admit C5-2.5c as the primary speculative-decoding Q4 break-even rider, C5-2.5b as its proposal-work secondary, and C5-2.5d as a mandatory contamination control. Preserve C5-2.5a in the deliberative bank as a deferred candidate rider only; it is not a standalone campaign commitment before a prospective cross-mechanism design is affordable. All four retain the evaluation&#39;s exact ceilings and forbidden upgrades, and C-023-OUTPUT-IDENTITY is binding.</li> <li>Admit C5-2.11 as the on-device MLX quantized-KV candidate and attach it to C5-2.4, C5-1.12, and C-023-QUALITY-EQUIV-QUANT. Preserve C5-2.12, C5-2.13, and C5-2.14 only as candidate riders on the existing context/KV-growth, prompt-cache/replay, and Q4/AP-1 homes.</li> <li>Admit one new canonical RQ row, RQ-AXI-HYBRID-PAIR, at an L2 named-pair ceiling. Attach the attention/context-slope and module-attribution refinements to existing rows. Record kernel/backend provenance as amendments to C5-1.8, C5-2.7, and C5-3.3, not new theses.</li> <li>Keep the roadmap&#39;s do-not-fold set out of the canonical row set. Its negative dispositions and all unresolved feasibility questions remain in the stream ledger, including explicit <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> markers. Intake does not convert an unresolved runtime, model-pair, adapter, or device-fit question into a capstone commitment.</li> </ol> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Mint every evaluated suggestion as an independent live question. Rejected: it duplicates existing homes, imports unidentifiable mechanism claims, and violates D-070&#39;s single-Q4-thesis posture.</li> <li>Admit only the top three ranked items. Rejected: the lower-cost controls, riders, and provenance amendments prevent predictable attribution errors without creating independent theses.</li> <li>Apply the roadmap&#39;s ranked fold-in and explicit exclusions. Chosen by Ed.</li> </ol> <p>Considerations: this is research-agenda intake, not campaign scheduling or evidence promotion. Every admitted candidate/rider remains floor-gated, earliest-phase tagged, capped at L2 unless an already-existing parent row&#39;s separate machinery says otherwise, and subject to its named forbidden upgrade. The published corpus remains claim-evidence-flagged; no fixture, runtime feasibility result, or registry entry is live energy evidence. D-070 remains the authority for Ed&#39;s axis commitments and quiet-Mac ordering.</p> <p>Revisit triggers: a relevant <strong>NEEDS-WEB</strong> feasibility finding lands; a named runtime/pair becomes unsupported; P2-015 floors make a predeclared effect undetectable; or Ed changes the D-070 commitment set. Revisit by amending the owning row and this decision&#39;s ledger, never by silently promoting an excluded candidate.</p> <span id="d-076"></span><h2 id="d-076-site-capacity-right-sizing-aud-wo-039-review-measured-first-budgets">D-076: Site capacity right-sizing (AUD-WO-039 review) — measured-first budgets</h2> <p>Date: 2026-07-17/18. Owner: lead under Ed&#39;s &quot;host the brief&quot; directive (the capacity decision event AUD-WO-039 fenced on). Ruling, encoded in tests with PR #76: the 1 MiB Lakebed hard cap is inviolate; the measured-artifact budget is 1,000,000 B (measured mode via the pinned validator, SITE-02 loud-discovery discipline); the 943,718 B conservative-estimate guard remains ONLY as fallback when measured mode is unavailable (estimator overshoot documented ~4.3% on identical input). WO-039 preservation boundary held: no advisor-facing page, navigation, provenance, or deep link trimmed. Current measured artifact 961,210 B. Revisit trigger: measured artifact within 24 KB of the hard cap forces the next right-sizing review before any addition.</p> <span id="d-077"></span><h2 id="d-077-environment-guard-idle-admission-and-cooldown-v2">D-077: Environment guard, idle admission, and cooldown v2</h2> <ul> <li>Date: 2026-07-17</li> <li>Status: accepted</li> <li>Phase: 2 / measurement</li> </ul> <p>Context: a Ventura video screensaver compositing on an awake display was identified as a material, repeatable contaminant. The affected windows showed about 50% GPU duty and were already detected by the existing <code>idle_window_suspect</code> thresholds. The campaign preflight, per-run admission, and D-014 cooldown nevertheless lacked one shared environment policy, exact override custody, and a sustained-window implementation. In particular, the old cooldown could release after one 5-second sub-window even though the contract called for a rolling 30-second recovery window.</p> <p>Options considered:</p> <ol> <li>Treat doctor output as a quietness certificate and continue to rely on operator judgment between members. Rejected: a point-in-time advisory cannot certify the later measured window and cannot enforce fixed-n admission.</li> <li>Change persistent display/screensaver preferences or allow contaminated members to be skipped or waived. Rejected: campaign preparation must not mutate host policy, and outcome-dependent skipping/waiving would break the fixed-n design and conceal the contamination.</li> <li>Use a hash-bound campaign-policy sidecar, an enforcing campaign preflight, per-run idle admission with one evidence-bearing retry, and cooldown v2 with frozen clean-anchor fallback. Chosen.</li> </ol> <p>Decision:</p> <ul> <li>A shared pure evaluator owns environment findings. Doctor consumes it only advisorily. <code>run_campaign.py</code> consumes it enforcingly after taking the campaign lock and before member 1. Critical unknowns fail closed. Load average is recorded as evidence but is never a member-admission gate.</li> <li>The production quiet-Mac policy requires AC power with an externally connected source, low-power mode off, all online displays asleep, the screensaver disengaged, and Nominal thermal pressure. Quiet-mode arming is explicit and transient: countdown, <code>pmset displaysleepnow</code>, then a complete re-probe. Persistent settings are never changed.</li> <li>An environment override must name the exact snapshot and findings digests it acknowledges. It is recorded as an override, never a waiver, and makes every resulting member universally claim-ineligible.</li> <li>Per-run idle admission reuses the validated <code>idle_window_suspect == false</code> threshold. It permits exactly one fully evidenced retry with distinct raw artifacts. Persistent awake-display, screensaver, or unknown critical state aborts immediately. Production aborts after retry; the exploratory-only <code>flag</code> path completes the fixed-n member but stamps the unwaivable <code>environment_admission_failed</code> reason on gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims. There is no skip action.</li> <li>Cooldown v2 amends D-014: recovery requires a complete, duration-weighted, sustained 30-second evidence window; the one-sided rule is <code>rolling_mean &lt;= reference * (1 + tolerance)</code>, so a below-reference window is recovered. Nominal thermal state is conjunctive. A calibrated absolute ceiling, when configured, is only an additional upper cap. A preceding baseline is reference-eligible only when its idle window is clean, critical environment checks passed, and policy/environment provenance is present. Otherwise the campaign uses one frozen clean anchor (NEG-8 reference start when present, else the first admission-passing baseline), records its provenance, never updates it from later outcomes, and fails closed when no eligible reference or anchor exists. Historical recovered rows are not reinterpreted.</li> <li>The policy owner is a strictly typed, byte-hashed sidecar under <code>configs/campaign_policies/</code>; policy version and SHA-256 are copied into each governed bundle. Campaign execution defaults to the production sidecar. Direct <code>joulewise run</code> without a sidecar retains legacy non-enforcing behavior. All bundle/config additions are nullable or omission-serialized; legacy normalized config bytes and hashes are unchanged.</li> <li>This amends D-057&#39;s stable claim-reason vocabulary by adding <code>environment_admission_failed</code> and <code>environment_override</code>. Both are universal and unwaivable for gross-energy, idle-subtracted-energy, and throughput claims.</li> </ul> <p>Considerations: environment admission is measurement-apparatus integrity, not post-hoc data cleaning. Duration weighting prevents irregular sub-window cadence from manufacturing coverage. Frozen-anchor provenance prevents a contaminated or outcome-selected member from quietly becoming the campaign&#39;s new recovery reference. The doctor remains useful as an early advisor without claiming more than its snapshot can prove.</p> <p>Consequences: campaign and bundle contracts gain policy/preflight/admission provenance, environment snapshots gain nullable display/screensaver/HID fields plus a post-run observation, and D-014&#39;s recovery wording is governed by cooldown v2 for new evidence. This decision is separate from AUD-WO-033, which remains behavior-preserving; D-077 intentionally changes future measurement admission and cooldown behavior and does not reinterpret sealed historical bundles.</p> <p>Revisit when: live quiet-window validation contradicts the defensive <code>pmset -g systemstate</code> display parser; calibrated platform data justifies an absolute ceiling; or a new platform cannot expose an equivalent critical probe without privilege.</p> <p>Fix-round amendment (2026-07-18): review found that summing sub-window durations as the completeness test made small inter-probe gaps reject an otherwise complete wall-clock window. Cooldown v2 now requires both a retained wall-clock span of at least <code>sustained_window_s</code> and captured coverage of at least <code>coverage_fraction * sustained_window_s</code>, with <code>coverage_fraction</code> defaulting to 0.8 and recorded in thresholds, trace rows, and release evidence. The same fix round made the existing frozen-reference rule operational for controller repetitions, attached cooldown evidence to each physical repetition (and each AXI entry), froze the first eligible repetition in execution order, re-probed the full governed environment per repetition, and added a guard observation after every idle capture. Environment-preflight early exits now retain a terminal campaign verdict; missing screensaver defaults domains use the macOS 20-minute default; and the two D-077 claim barriers are registered in the canonical reducer vocabulary. These are defect corrections to the accepted policy, not new policy alternatives.</p> <nav class="doc-meta" aria-label="Decision log parts"><span>Decision log parts:</span> <a href="decision_log.html">Recent</a> · <strong aria-current="page">Archive 1</strong></nav> </div> </div> </main> <footer class="site"> <div class="inner"> <span>JouleWise · github.com/mpmdw/JouleWise</span> <span>docs/decision_log.md · commit 1af9f92 + uncommitted · regenerate: <span class="mono">python3 scripts/build_site.py</span></span> </div> </footer> </body> </html>
