  1249	def _diagnostics_are_nonpublishing(
  1250	    value: object, *, diagnostic_context: bool = False
  1251	) -> bool:
  1252	    if isinstance(value, Mapping):
  1253	        is_diagnostic = diagnostic_context or (
  1254	            value.get("label") == "repeatability_diagnostic"
  1255	        )
  1256	        if is_diagnostic and value.get("published_claim_floor") is not False:
  1257	            return False
  1258	        for key, child in value.items():
  1259	            if key == "published_claim_floor" and child is not False:
  1260	                return False
  1261	            if not _diagnostics_are_nonpublishing(
  1262	                child,
  1263	                diagnostic_context=key in {
  1264	                    "point_floor_diagnostic",
  1265	                    "point_floor_diagnostics",
  1266	                },
  1267	            ):
  1268	                return False
  1269	    elif isinstance(value, list):
  1270	        return all(_diagnostics_are_nonpublishing(child) for child in value)
  1271	    return True

  1274	def pre_registration_gate(
  1275	    *,
  1276	    plan: Mapping[str, Any],
  1277	    plan_sha256: str,

  1281	    """Enforce the ratified mint-1 literals before any builder call."""

  1287	        or plan.get("calibration_scope") != PLAN_DECLARED_SCOPE

  1292	            "pre-registration gate: components require distinct a10/window_c roots"
  1293	        )

  1295	        absolute.whole_window_evaluation_basis_sha256

  1298	        != WINDOW_C_EVALUATION_BASIS_SHA256

  1302	        absolute.evaluation_basis_member_count != A10_EVALUATION_BASIS_MEMBERS
  1303	        or comparative.evaluation_basis_member_count
  1304	        != WINDOW_C_EVALUATION_BASIS_MEMBERS
  1305	    ):
  1306	        raise MintError("pre-registration gate: evaluation-basis member count mismatch")
  1307	    if (
  1308	        len(_spec_member_ids(absolute.spec)) != A10_SPEC_MEMBERS
  1309	        or len(_spec_member_ids(comparative.spec)) != WINDOW_C_SPEC_MEMBERS

  1311	        raise MintError("pre-registration gate: extraction-spec membership mismatch")

  1425	def _comparative_blocks(
  1426	    component: AuthenticatedComponent,
  1427	) -> tuple[list[Mapping[str, Any]], list[float]]:
  1428	    blocks = component.spec_cell["blocks"]

  1430	    result: list[Mapping[str, Any]] = []
  1431	    deltas: list[float] = []
  1432	    for spec_block in blocks:
  1433	        block_id = spec_block["block_id"]
  1434	        ids = spec_block["members"]
  1435	        values = {
  1436	            position: member_by_id[ids[position]].metric_value_j
  1437	            for position in _ABBA_POSITIONS
  1438	        }

  1442	        deltas.append(delta)
  1443	        result.append(
  1444	            {
  1445	                "block_id": block_id,
  1446	                "executed_labels": ["A", "B", "B", "A"],
  1447	                "members": [
  1448	                    {
  1449	                        "position": position,

  1619	def _resolve_plan_path(floor_path: Path, relative_path: object) -> Path:
  1620	    relative = _safe_relative_posix(
  1621	        relative_path, "artifact.provenance.calibration_plan.relative_path"
  1622	    )
  1623	    root = floor_path.parent.resolve()
  1624	    candidate = (root / relative).resolve()
  1625	    try:
  1626	        candidate.relative_to(root)
  1627	    except ValueError as exc:
  1628	        raise MintError("calibration plan escapes the artifact root") from exc
  1629	    return candidate

  1632	def _record_rows(component_name: str, cell: Mapping[str, Any]) -> list[Mapping]:

  1635	        return []
  1636	    if component_name == "absolute":
  1637	        rows = record.get("bundle_observations")

  1639	    result: list[Mapping] = []
  1640	    blocks = record.get("blocks")
  1641	    if isinstance(blocks, list):
  1642	        for block in blocks:
  1643	            members = block.get("members") if isinstance(block, Mapping) else None
  1644	            if isinstance(members, list):
  1645	                result.extend(row for row in members if isinstance(row, Mapping))
  1646	    return result

  1859	def render_single_count_statement(artifact: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
  1860	    """Render the convenience prose only from the canonical artifact object."""
  1861	
  1862	    expected = attribution_single_count_discipline()
  1863	    carried: list[Mapping[str, Any]] = []
  1864	    for cell in artifact.get("cells", []):
  1865	        if isinstance(cell, Mapping) and isinstance(
  1866	            cell.get("single_count_discipline"), Mapping
  1867	        ):
  1868	            carried.append(cell["single_count_discipline"])
  1869	    for group in artifact.get("transport_groups", []):
  1870	        if isinstance(group, Mapping) and isinstance(
  1871	            group.get("single_count_discipline"), Mapping
  1872	        ):
  1873	            carried.append(group["single_count_discipline"])
  1874	    if not carried:
  1875	        raise MintError("artifact does not carry a single-count discipline object")
  1876	    if any(dict(value) != expected for value in carried):
  1877	        raise MintError("artifact single-count discipline is not canonical")
  1878	    return (
  1879	        f"{expected['statement']}. "
  1880	        f"Formula: {expected['effective_clearable_effect_formula']}; "
  1881	        f"floor role: {expected['floor_role']}; "
  1882	        f"claim-side role: {expected['claim_side_bound_role']}; "
  1883	        f"claim-side source: {expected['claim_side_bound_source']}.\n"
  1884	    )

  1887	def _exclusive_write(path: Path, payload: bytes) -> None:
  1888	    path = Path(path)
  1889	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
  1890	    try:
  1891	        descriptor = os.open(
  1892	            path,
  1893	            os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL,
  1894	            0o644,
  1895	        )
  1896	    except FileExistsError as exc:
  1897	        raise MintError(f"refusing to overwrite existing output: {path}") from exc
  1898	    try:
  1899	        with os.fdopen(descriptor, "wb") as handle:
  1900	            handle.write(payload)
  1901	            handle.flush()
  1902	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
  1903	    except Exception:
  1904	        try:
  1905	            path.unlink()
  1906	        except OSError:
  1907	            pass
  1908	        raise
  1909

  1911	def write_outputs_exclusive(
  1912	    artifact: Mapping[str, Any],
  1913	    floor_path: Path,
  1914	    statement_path: Path,
  1915	) -> None:
  1916	    """Write the artifact and convenience statement with O_EXCL semantics."""
  1917	
  1918	    floor_path = Path(floor_path)
  1919	    statement_path = Path(statement_path)
  1920	    if floor_path == statement_path:
  1921	        raise MintError("artifact and statement outputs must differ")
  1922	    if floor_path.exists() or statement_path.exists():
  1923	        existing = floor_path if floor_path.exists() else statement_path
  1924	        raise MintError(f"refusing to overwrite existing output: {existing}")
  1925	    artifact_payload = (
  1926	        json.dumps(artifact, indent=2, sort_keys=True, allow_nan=False) + "\n"
  1927	    ).encode("utf-8")
  1928	    statement_payload = render_single_count_statement(artifact).encode("utf-8")
  1929	    _exclusive_write(floor_path, artifact_payload)
  1930	    try:
  1931	        _exclusive_write(statement_path, statement_payload)
  1932	    except Exception:
  1933	        try:
  1934	            floor_path.unlink()
  1935	        except OSError:
  1936	            pass
  1937	        raise

  1940	def mint_floor_artifact(
  1941	    *,
  1942	    artifact_id: str,
  1943	    floor_path: Path,
  1944	    statement_path: Path,
  1945	    calibration_plan_path: Path,
  1946	    calibration_plan_relative_path: str,
  1947	    absolute_paths: ComponentPaths,
  1948	    comparative_paths: ComponentPaths,
  1949	    project_commit: str,
  1950	    project_tree_state: str,
  1951	    strict_validator: StrictValidator,
  1952	    consumption_semantics_id: str | None = None,
  1953	    calibration_ledger_snapshot: CalibrationLedgerSnapshot | None = None,
  1954	) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
  1955	    """Authenticate, gate, construct, rebind, validate, and write mint #1."""
  1956	
  1957	    plan, plan_raw = _load_json_object(calibration_plan_path, "calibration plan")
  1958	    plan_sha256 = _sha256(plan_raw)
  1959	    if calibration_ledger_snapshot is None:

  1961	        cutoff = (
  1962	            acceptance.get("ledger_cutoff")
  1963	            if isinstance(acceptance, Mapping)
  1964	            else None
  1965	        )
  1966	        calibration_ledger_snapshot = load_calibration_ledger_snapshot(
  1967	            baseline_sequence=(
  1968	                cutoff.get("sequence") if isinstance(cutoff, Mapping) else None
  1969	            ),
  1970	            baseline_digest=(
  1971	                cutoff.get("head_digest") if isinstance(cutoff, Mapping) else None
  1972	            ),
  1973	        )
  1974	    absolute = _authenticate_component(
  1975	        absolute_paths,
  1976	        expected_cell_id=A10_CELL_ID,
  1977	        expected_basis_sha256=A10_EVALUATION_BASIS_SHA256,
  1978	        strict_validator=strict_validator,
  1979	        expected_consumption_semantics_id=consumption_semantics_id,
  1980	        calibration_ledger_snapshot=calibration_ledger_snapshot,
  1981	    )
  1982	    comparative = _authenticate_component(
  1983	        comparative_paths,
  1984	        expected_cell_id=WINDOW_C_CELL_ID,
  1985	        expected_basis_sha256=WINDOW_C_EVALUATION_BASIS_SHA256,
  1986	        strict_validator=strict_validator,
  1987	        expected_consumption_semantics_id=consumption_semantics_id,
  1988	        calibration_ledger_snapshot=calibration_ledger_snapshot,
  1989	    )
  1990	    artifact = mint_authenticated_artifact(
  1991	        artifact_id=artifact_id,
  1992	        plan=plan,
  1993	        plan_sha256=plan_sha256,
  1994	        calibration_plan_relative_path=calibration_plan_relative_path,
  1995	        absolute=absolute,
  1996	        comparative=comparative,
  1997	        project_commit=project_commit,
  1998	        project_tree_state=project_tree_state,
  1999	    )
  2000	    cache_keys: list[tuple[str, str, tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]]] = []
  2001	    artifact_cell = artifact["cells"][0]
  2002	    for component_name, component, root in (
  2003	        ("absolute", absolute, absolute_paths.evidence_root),
  2004	        ("comparative", comparative, comparative_paths.evidence_root),
  2005	    ):
  2006	        rows = _record_rows(component_name, artifact_cell)
  2007	        cache_key = _binding_cache_key(
  2008	            root,
  2009	            component.whole_window_evaluation_basis_sha256,
  2010	            rows,
  2011	        )
  2012	        _BINDING_SUMMARY_CACHE[cache_key] = {
  2013	            member.bundle_id: member.summary for member in component.members
  2014	        }
  2015	        cache_keys.append(cache_key)
  2016	    try:
  2017	        bind_floor_artifact_evidence(
  2018	            artifact,
  2019	            floor_path,
  2020	            {
  2021	                absolute.evidence_root_id: absolute_paths.evidence_root,
  2022	                comparative.evidence_root_id: comparative_paths.evidence_root,
  2023	            },
  2024	            strict_validator=strict_validator,
  2025	            calibration_ledger_snapshot=calibration_ledger_snapshot,
  2026	        )
  2027	    finally:
  2028	        for cache_key in cache_keys:
  2029	            _BINDING_SUMMARY_CACHE.pop(cache_key, None)
  2030	    if validate_floor_artifact(artifact) != []:
  2031	        raise MintError("post-bind artifact validation failed")
  2032	    write_outputs_exclusive(artifact, floor_path, statement_path)
  2033	    return artifact

  2099	                order_manifest_path=args.window_c_order_manifest,
  2100	                calibration_cell_id=WINDOW_C_CELL_ID,
  2101	                expected_kind="comparative",

  2110	    except MintError as exc:

  2997	# Conservative regime-transport refusal rule (pure)

  3000	_CONSUMER_IDENTITY_FIELDS = ("backend", "metric", "window_class", "stack_identity_sha256")
  3001	_CONSUMER_ENVELOPE_FIELDS = _ENVELOPE_FIELDS
  3002	_BOUND_TERM_REASONS = {

  3004	    "interpolation_bound_j": "interpolation_harder_than_calibration",

  3009	def transport_refusal_reasons(
  3010	    consumer: Mapping,
  3011	    group: Mapping,
  3012	    source_cells_by_id: Optional[Mapping] = None,
  3013	    *,
  3014	    artifact_sha256: Optional[str] = None,
  3015	    expected_artifact_sha256: Optional[str] = None,
  3016	    artifact_schema_valid: bool = True,
  3017	) -> tuple:
  3018	    """Pure Unit 6.2 transport check; empty tuple means transport is allowed.
  3019	
  3020	    A floor cell/group must refuse to bound a different regime unless every
  3021	    predeclared conservative check passes: exact stack identity, predeclared
  3022	    condition family, consumer power/duration inside the measured bracket,
  3023	    and consumer cadence/clock/interpolation/drift evidence no worse than the
  3024	    composed calibration envelope. Missing or unknown consumer evidence
  3025	    refuses (``consumer_term_unknown``); nothing is extrapolated and no ad hoc
  3026	    margin is added. Optional artifact hash and schema-validation inputs make
  3027	    the two artifact-level refusal codes reachable before transport checks.
  3028	    """
  3029	    reasons: list = []
  3030	
  3031	    def refuse(reason: str) -> None:
  3032	        if reason not in reasons:
  3033	            reasons.append(reason)
  3034	
  3035	    if not artifact_schema_valid:
  3036	        refuse("artifact_schema_invalid")
  3037	    if expected_artifact_sha256 is not None and artifact_sha256 != expected_artifact_sha256:
  3038	        refuse("artifact_hash_mismatch")
  3039	
  3040	    # Group completeness / source health (when the source cells are supplied).
  3041	    source_ids = group.get("source_cell_ids") or []
  3042	    if not source_ids:
  3043	        refuse("transport_group_incomplete")
  3044	    elif source_cells_by_id is not None:
  3045	        for cell_id in source_ids:
  3046	            cell = source_cells_by_id.get(cell_id)
  3047	            if cell is None:
  3048	                refuse("cell_missing")
  3049	                continue
  3050	            status = cell.get("eligibility", {}).get("status")
  3051	            if status == "stale":
  3052	                refuse("cell_stale")
  3053	            elif status != "claim_ready":
  3054	                refuse("cell_not_claim_ready")
  3055	
  3056	    # Exact stack identity; any invariant difference is a stack mismatch.
  3057	    for field in _CONSUMER_IDENTITY_FIELDS:
  3058	        value = consumer.get(field)
  3059	        if value is None:
  3060	            refuse("consumer_term_unknown")
  3061	        elif value != group.get(field):
  3062	            refuse("stack_mismatch")
  3063	
  3064	    # Predeclared condition family (id + hash must both match).
  3065	    family_id = consumer.get("condition_family_id")
  3066	    family_sha = consumer.get("condition_family_sha256")
  3067	    if family_id is None or family_sha is None:
  3068	        refuse("consumer_term_unknown")

  3070	        allowed = group.get("allowed_consumer_condition_families") or []
  3071	        if not any(
  3072	            family.get("condition_family_id") == family_id
  3073	            and family.get("condition_family_sha256") == family_sha
  3074	            for family in allowed
  3075	        ):
  3076	            refuse("condition_not_predeclared")
  3077	
  3078	    envelope = group.get("stress_envelope") or {}
  3079	    values = {}
  3080	    for field in _CONSUMER_ENVELOPE_FIELDS:
  3081	        value = consumer.get(field)
  3082	        if not _is_number(value):
  3083	            refuse("consumer_term_unknown")
  3084	        else:
  3085	            values[field] = value
  3086	
  3087	    def _have(*fields) -> bool:
  3088	        return all(f in values for f in fields)
  3089	
  3090	    if _have("mean_power_w_min", "mean_power_w_max"):
  3091	        if values["mean_power_w_min"] < envelope.get("mean_power_w_min", math.inf) or values[
  3092	            "mean_power_w_max"
  3093	        ] > envelope.get("mean_power_w_max", -math.inf):
  3094	            refuse("power_outside_calibrated_envelope")
  3095	    if _have("window_duration_s_min", "window_duration_s_max"):
  3096	        if values["window_duration_s_min"] < envelope.get("window_duration_s_min", math.inf) or values[
  3097	            "window_duration_s_max"
  3098	        ] > envelope.get("window_duration_s_max", -math.inf):
  3099	            refuse("duration_outside_calibrated_envelope")
  3100	    if _have("p95_sample_gap_s_max") and values["p95_sample_gap_s_max"] > envelope.get(
  3101	        "p95_sample_gap_s_max", -math.inf
  3102	    ):
  3103	        refuse("cadence_harder_than_calibration")
  3104	    if _have("bracketing_sample_gap_s_max") and values["bracketing_sample_gap_s_max"] > envelope.get(
  3105	        "bracketing_sample_gap_s_max", -math.inf
  3106	    ):
  3107	        refuse("cadence_harder_than_calibration")
  3108	    if _have("cadence_ratio_min") and values["cadence_ratio_min"] < envelope.get("cadence_ratio_min", math.inf):
  3109	        refuse("cadence_harder_than_calibration")
  3110	
  3111	    group_terms = envelope.get("bound_term_maxima") or {}
  3112	    consumer_terms = consumer.get("bound_terms") or {}
  3113	    for term, reason in _BOUND_TERM_REASONS.items():
  3114	        entry = consumer_terms.get(term)
  3115	        if entry is None:
  3116	            refuse("consumer_term_unknown")
  3117	            continue
  3118	        applicability = entry.get("applicability")
  3119	        if applicability == "not_applicable":
  3120	            continue
  3121	        if applicability == "unknown" or not _is_number(entry.get("maximum")):
  3122	            refuse("consumer_term_unknown")
  3123	            continue
  3124	        group_max = group_terms.get(term)
  3125	        if group_max is None or entry["maximum"] > group_max:
  3126	            refuse(reason)

  3129	    return tuple(reasons)

   150	nonparametric one-sided 95/95 tolerance bound needs
   151	`ceil(log(0.05) / log(0.95)) = 59` samples before the maximum has 95% coverage.
   152	The false-effect guard floor instead combines the largest observed false effect
   153	with a Student-t prediction bound for one new observation or contrast. It gives
   154	an operational guard against repeatability and ordering artifacts under the
   155	calibrated condition family. It does not promise nonparametric 95/95 coverage,
   156	does not validate unobserved thermal/controller states, and does not replace
   157	backend systematic or drift bounds.
   158	
   159	### Pinset-Derived Evidence-Root Authentication
   160	
   161	`validate_floor_artifact` authenticates each component's
   162	`evidence_root_id` against the artifact family's reviewed floor-mint pinset.
   163	The allowed set is the unique set of exact literals already stored at
   164	`absolute.evidence_root_id` and `comparative.evidence_root_id` in that
   165	pinset. There is no wildcard, pattern-based allowance, nonempty-string
   166	fallback, or duplicate root-list field. Adding a future family or root is a
   167	reviewed pinset-data change; it is not a validator code change.
   168	
   169	The artifact-to-pinset join uses only this existing identity tuple:
   170	
   171	1. `provenance.mint_tool_version`;
   172	2. `provenance.calibration_plan.plan_id`; and
   173	3. `provenance.calibration_plan.sha256`.
   174	
   175	The ordinary library validator resolves that tuple against the v1 pinsets in
   176	`scripts/floor_mint_pinsets/`. Repository discovery accepts only regular
   177	`*.json` files that are not symlinks; a symlink, non-regular entry, unreadable
   178	file, malformed JSON document, duplicate-key document, or document outside the
   179	closed v1 schema makes resolution refuse rather than silently disappearing
   180	from the candidate set.
   181	
   182	The public explicit route is
   183	`validate_floor_artifact(artifact, pinset_path=...,`
   184	`expected_pinset_sha256=...)`. Both arguments are required together. The
   185	library itself rejects symlinks and non-regular files, re-reads the exact bytes,
   186	checks them against the expected digest, and parses only after that check. No
   187	public route accepts an already-parsed pinset mapping. The generalized mint
   188	passes its path and separately supplied expected SHA-256 through this route; it
   189	does not pass parsed content or rewrite a future family's root ids to mint-1
   190	labels. Resolution is fail-closed and produces these core findings:
   191	
   192	- zero matches: `artifact.pinset: no pinset matches artifact family identity`;
   193	- multiple matches: `artifact.pinset: multiple pinsets match artifact family identity`;
   194	- a component root outside the uniquely matched family's two pinned literals:
   195	  `cells[N].provenance.COMPONENT.evidence_root_id: not pinned by artifact family pinset`.
   196	
   197	Mint-1 behavior is frozen: `scripts/floor_mint_pinsets/mint1.json` remains
   198	byte-identical at SHA-256
   199	`4c58e64636863379f26bcf0fe03503ddfcf3bcf9bfa184fe0d385ca47b459a67`;
   200	its existing `a10` and `window_c` literals, artifact construction, and the
   201	original mint's final validation gate are unchanged. A valid mint-1 artifact
   202	therefore retains the exact finding bytes `[]`. This authentication route does
   203	not grant or restore any mint license. In particular, D-110 clause 3 remains a
   204	separate license gate; a future pinset can make a hypothetical artifact
   205	truthfully valid without authorizing that artifact to be minted or published.
   206	
   207	### Cell List
   208	
   209	The default target for Window A is `n = 10` strict-valid bundles per cell.
   210	That is feasible for request and phase cells at the expected 30-75 bundles per

   261	def _exact_mapping_keys(
   262	    value: object,
   263	    expected: set[str],
   264	    where: str,
   265	    errors: list[str],
   266	) -> bool:
   267	    if not isinstance(value, Mapping):
   268	        errors.append(f"{where}: must be an object")
   269	        return False
   270	    unknown = set(value) - expected
   271	    missing = expected - set(value)
   272	    for key in sorted(unknown):
   273	        errors.append(f"{where}: unrecognized key {key!r}")
   274	    for key in sorted(missing):
   275	        errors.append(f"{where}: missing key {key!r}")
   276	    return not unknown and not missing

   891	def _read_summary(
   892	    path: Path,
   893	) -> tuple[Mapping[str, Any] | None, str | None, str | None]:
   894	    if not path.is_dir():
   895	        return None, None, "bundle_missing"
   896	    summary_path = path / "summary_metrics.json"
   897	    try:
   898	        raw = summary_path.read_bytes()
   899	    except OSError:
   900	        return None, None, "summary_unreadable"
   901	    digest = hashlib.sha256(raw).hexdigest()
   902	    try:
   903	        # Strict UTF-8 only: json.loads on bytes auto-detects BOM/UTF-16/32,
   904	        # which would admit encodings the committed reader refused.
   905	        parsed = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
   906	    except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError):
   907	        return None, digest, "summary_unreadable"
   908	    if not isinstance(parsed, Mapping):
   909	        return None, digest, "summary_unreadable"
   910	    return parsed, digest, None

   913	def _finite(value: object) -> float | None:
   914	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
   915	        return None
   916	    converted = float(value)
   917	    return converted if math.isfinite(converted) else None

   920	def _member_metric_value(summary: Mapping[str, Any], metric: str) -> float | None:
   921	    if metric.startswith("phase_energy_j."):
   922	        phases = summary.get("phase_energy_j")
   923	        raw = phases.get(metric.split(".", 1)[1]) if isinstance(phases, Mapping) else None
   924	    else:
   925	        raw = summary.get(metric)
   926	    return _finite(raw)

  1248	def _validate_cap_hit_policy(cap_hit_policy: str) -> None:
  1249	    if cap_hit_policy != CAP_HIT_POLICY_EXCLUDE_SAME_SLOT:
  1250	        # Drift-term retention is predeclared but has no governed bound
  1251	        # source yet; anything else fails closed rather than inventing one.
  1252	        raise FloorExtractionError(
  1253	            f"unsupported cap-hit policy {cap_hit_policy!r}; only "
  1254	            f"{CAP_HIT_POLICY_EXCLUDE_SAME_SLOT!r} is governed"
  1255	        )

  1258	def _unique_bundle_ids(bundle_ids: Sequence[str]) -> None:
  1259	    seen: set[str] = set()
  1260	    for bundle_id in bundle_ids:
  1260	    for bundle_id in bundle_ids:
  1261	        if not isinstance(bundle_id, str) or not bundle_id:
  1262	            raise FloorExtractionError("member bundle_id must be a nonempty string")
  1263	        if bundle_id in seen:
  1264	            raise FloorExtractionError(
  1265	                f"duplicate member bundle_id {bundle_id!r}: pseudo-replication refused"
  1266	            )
  1267	        seen.add(bundle_id)

  1270	def extract_absolute_cell(
  1271	    *,
  1272	    cell_id: str,
  1273	    metric: str,
  1274	    window_class: str,
  1275	    members: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
  1276	    runs_root: Path,
  1277	    cooldowns: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]],
  1278	    cap_hit_policy: str = CAP_HIT_POLICY_EXCLUDE_SAME_SLOT,
  1279	    hash_bundles: bool = False,
  1280	    strict_validator: StrictValidator | None = None,
  1281	    consumption_session: AuthenticatedConsumptionSession | None = None,
  1282	) -> CellReport:
  1283	    """Extract one absolute D-054 cell under the audit gates."""
  1284	
  1285	    validator = strict_validator or _default_strict_validator
  1286	    metric, window_class = governed_cell_metric(metric, window_class)
  1287	    _validate_cap_hit_policy(cap_hit_policy)
  1288	    if not members:
  1289	        raise FloorExtractionError("absolute cell requires at least one member")
  1290	    slots = [str(row.get("slot", row.get("bundle_id", ""))) for row in members]
  1291	    if len(set(slots)) != len(slots):
  1292	        raise FloorExtractionError("absolute cell member slots must be unique")
  1293	    _unique_bundle_ids([str(row.get("bundle_id", "")) for row in members])

  1297	        reports.append(
  1298	            _evaluate_member(
  1299	                slot=slot,
  1300	                bundle_id=str(row["bundle_id"]),
  1301	                block_id=None,
  1302	                position=None,
  1303	                runs_root=runs_root,
  1304	                metric=metric,
  1305	                window_class=window_class,
  1306	                cooldowns=cooldowns,
  1307	                hash_bundles=hash_bundles,
  1308	                strict_validator=validator,
  1309	                consumption_session=consumption_session,
  1310	            )
  1311	        )
  1312	
  1313	    refusals: list[str] = []
  1314	    excluded_slots: list[str] = []
  1315	    fallback_exclusion_diagnostics: list[str] = []

  1323	                reason
  1324	                for reason in member.reasons

  1326	                not in {
  1327	                    ANCHOR_FALLBACK_MEMBER_REFUSAL,
  1328	                    "clock_anchor_unresolved",
  1329	                }
  1330	            )

  1344	    point_floor: FloorEstimate | None = None
  1345	    anchor_max: float | None = None
  1346	    if not refusals:
  1347	        if len(admitted) < 2:

  1349	            refusals.extend(fallback_exclusion_diagnostics)
  1350	        else:

  1407	def extract_comparative_cell(
  1408	    *,
  1409	    cell_id: str,
  1410	    metric: str,
  1411	    window_class: str,
  1412	    blocks: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]],
  1413	    runs_root: Path,
  1414	    cooldowns: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]],
  1415	    cap_hit_policy: str = CAP_HIT_POLICY_EXCLUDE_SAME_SLOT,
  1416	    hash_bundles: bool = False,
  1417	    strict_validator: StrictValidator | None = None,
  1418	    consumption_session: AuthenticatedConsumptionSession | None = None,
  1419	) -> CellReport:
  1420	    """Extract one comparative (ABBA) D-054 cell under the audit gates.
  1421	
  1422	    A cap-hit member excludes its WHOLE block (same-slot exclusion): the
  1423	    remaining three members of that block never contribute to any delta, and
  1424	    the comparative floor proceeds at n_blocks - 1 under the frozen
  1425	    small-sample guard.

  1428	    validator = strict_validator or _default_strict_validator
  1429	    metric, window_class = governed_cell_metric(metric, window_class)
  1430	    _validate_cap_hit_policy(cap_hit_policy)
  1431	    if not blocks:
  1432	        raise FloorExtractionError("comparative cell requires at least one block")
  1433	    block_ids = [str(block.get("block_id", "")) for block in blocks]
  1434	    if len(set(block_ids)) != len(block_ids) or "" in block_ids:
  1435	        raise FloorExtractionError("comparative blocks need unique nonempty block_ids")
  1436	    all_bundle_ids: list[str] = []
  1437	    for block in blocks:
  1438	        block_members = block.get("members")
  1439	        if not isinstance(block_members, Mapping) or set(block_members) != set(
  1440	            _ABBA_POSITIONS
  1441	        ):
  1442	            raise FloorExtractionError(
  1443	                "each ABBA block requires exactly the members A1/B1/B2/A2"
  1444	            )
  1445	        all_bundle_ids.extend(str(block_members[pos]) for pos in _ABBA_POSITIONS)
  1446	    _unique_bundle_ids(all_bundle_ids)
  1447	
  1448	    refusals: list[str] = []

     2	"""Fail-closed detection-floor extraction CLI (2026-07-19 audit T0.4/T0.6).
     3	
     4	Runs :mod:`joulewise.floor_extraction` over one runs root and one extraction
     5	spec, writing a ``joulewise.detection_floor_extraction.v1`` report.
     6	
     7	Exit codes:
     8	
     9	* ``0`` — every cell extracted under all governed gates;
    10	* ``1`` — the report was written but at least one cell refused (fail-closed
    11	  evidence refusals are recorded per member/cell, never silently dropped);
    12	* ``2`` — process-input error (bad spec, bad paths); no report is written.
    13	
    14	Per D-078, corpora recorded before the trace-time-anchor fix refuse
    15	mechanically (their wires cannot carry anchor-shift envelopes); this tool
    16	never publishes a claim-bearing floor from them.
    17	"""
    18	
    19	from __future__ import annotations
    20	
    21	import argparse
    22	import json
    23	import sys
    24	from pathlib import Path
    25	
    26	REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
    27	if str(REPO_ROOT) not in sys.path:
    28	    sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO_ROOT))

    32	    MAX_BRACKET_CONSUMPTION_SEMANTICS_ID,

    34	    SALVAGE_DANGLER_CONSUMPTION_SEMANTICS_ID,
    35	)

    38	def _stored_bundle_containing(path: Path) -> Path | None:
    39	    """Return the finalized bundle ancestor of a prospective output path."""
    40	
    41	    resolved = path.resolve(strict=False)
    42	    for parent in resolved.parents:
    43	        if (parent / "summary_metrics.json").is_file():
    44	            return parent
    45	    return None
    46	
    47	
    48	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    49	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    50	    parser.add_argument(
    51	        "--runs-root",
    52	        required=True,
    53	        type=Path,
    54	        help="corpus root containing the member bundles and campaign_manifests/",
    55	    )
    56	    parser.add_argument(
    57	        "--spec",
    58	        required=True,
    59	        type=Path,
    60	        help="joulewise.detection_floor_extraction_spec.v1 JSON document",
    61	    )

    63	        "--out",

    74	        ),

    84	    parser.add_argument(
    85	        "--consumption-semantics-id",
    86	        default=None,
    87	        choices=(
    88	            MINTED_CONSUMPTION_SEMANTICS_ID,
    89	            MAX_BRACKET_CONSUMPTION_SEMANTICS_ID,
    90	            SALVAGE_DANGLER_CONSUMPTION_SEMANTICS_ID,
    91	        ),
    92	        help="exact whole-window verdict consumption semantics",
    93	    )
    94	    parser.add_argument(
    95	        "--hash-bundles",
    96	        action="store_true",
    97	        help="record complete-bundle and config sha256 pins per member",
    98	    )
    99	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
   100	
   101	    if (args.evaluation_basis_sha256 is None) != (
   102	        args.consumption_semantics_id is None
   103	    ):
   104	        parser.error(
   105	            "--evaluation-basis-sha256 and --consumption-semantics-id are required together"
   106	        )
   107	    if args.evaluation_basis_sha256 is not None and not (
   108	        len(args.evaluation_basis_sha256) == 64
   109	        and all(
   110	            character in "0123456789abcdef"

   113	    ):

   119	        print(f"error: cannot read extraction spec: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)

   121	    if not args.runs_root.is_dir():

   123	        return 2
   124	    if args.out.exists():
   125	        print(
   126	            f"error: refusing to overwrite existing extraction artifact: {args.out}",
   127	            file=sys.stderr,
   128	        )
   129	        return 2
   130	    bundle_ancestor = _stored_bundle_containing(args.out)
   131	    if bundle_ancestor is not None:
   132	        print(
   133	            "error: extraction output must be outside the immutable stored "
   134	            f"run bundle: {bundle_ancestor}",
   135	            file=sys.stderr,
   136	        )
   137	        return 2
   138	
   139	    try:
   140	        report = extract_cells(
   141	            args.runs_root,
   142	            spec,
   143	            manifest_id=args.manifest_id,
   144	            evaluation_basis_sha256=args.evaluation_basis_sha256,
   145	            consumption_semantics_id=args.consumption_semantics_id,
   146	            hash_bundles=args.hash_bundles,
   147	        )
   148	    except FloorExtractionError as exc:
   149	        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
   150	        return 2
   151	
   152	    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   153	    try:
   154	        with args.out.open("x", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
   155	            handle.write(json.dumps(report, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
   156	    except FileExistsError:
   157	        print(
   158	            f"error: refusing to overwrite existing extraction artifact: {args.out}",
   159	            file=sys.stderr,
   160	        )
   161	        return 2
   162	    refused = [
   163	        cell["cell_id"] for cell in report["cells"] if not cell["extractable"]
   164	    ]
   165	    omitted = [
   166	        row["bundle_id"] for row in report.get("spec_membership_refusals", [])
   167	    ]
   168	    if refused or omitted:
   169	        if refused:
   170	            print(
   171	                "refused cells (fail-closed): " + ", ".join(sorted(refused)),
   172	                file=sys.stderr,
   173	            )
   174	        if omitted:
   175	            print(
   176	                "campaign members omitted from spec (fail-closed): "
   177	                + ", ".join(sorted(omitted)),
   178	                file=sys.stderr,
   179	            )

   651	def reader_throughput_tokens_s(summary: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> float | None:
   652	    """Return the governed N-1 reader-facing throughput, never the legacy field."""
   653	
   654	    value = (

   658	        return None
   659	    converted = float(value)
   660	    return converted if math.isfinite(converted) and converted >= 0.0 else None

  1752	    # high-scatter bundle, shrink the false-effect floor); it refuses the whole
  1753	    # extraction rather than proceeding at an unrecorded n-1.
  1754	    #
  1755	    # The completeness check is SCOPED to addressed campaigns, not the whole
  1756	    # runs_root union.  A single runs_root routinely holds several calibration
  1757	    # campaign manifests (all ``analysis_manifest_id`` null) spanning different
  1758	    # metric/window families; a legitimate per-cell/per-metric spec names only
  1759	    # its own campaign's members.  Requiring the union would force one omnibus
  1760	    # spec covering every sibling campaign under the runs_root, which is not the
  1761	    # per-cell contract.  Each resolved cooldown row carries the manifest it was
  1762	    # recovered from (``campaign_cooldown_evidence`` is the ONE join model — we
  1763	    # reuse its attribution, never re-read manifests here); a campaign is
  1764	    # "addressed" iff the spec references at least one of its members.  Members
  1765	    # whose provenance is ambiguous/unattributable (``manifest`` null, e.g.
  1766	    # conflicting duplicate records — the SAME bundle_id claimed by two campaign
  1767	    # manifests, or duplicate rows within one) cannot be tied to a campaign, so
  1768	    # we cannot prove they do NOT belong to a campaign the spec addresses.  A
  1769	    # referenced unattributable member still faces its own member gate, but an
  1770	    # OMITTED unattributable member would silently escape the completeness check

  1773	    # any resolved null-manifest cooldown the spec does not reference refuses the

  1886	def _spec_referenced_bundle_ids(cells: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]]) -> set[str]:

  1890	    for cell in cells:

  1894	        if isinstance(members, list):

  1898	                    referenced.add(bundle_id)

  1900	        if isinstance(blocks, list):
  1901	            for block in blocks:
  1902	                block_members = (
  1903	                    block.get("members") if isinstance(block, Mapping) else None
  1904	                )
  1905	                if isinstance(block_members, Mapping):
  1906	                    for bundle_id in block_members.values():
  1907	                        if isinstance(bundle_id, str) and bundle_id:
  1908	                            referenced.add(bundle_id)

   378	class AuthenticatedConsumptionSession:
   379	    """One collection-scoped authenticated max-bracket consumption session.
   380	
   381	    The session owns one immutable D-109 ledger snapshot and bracket
   382	    authentication, computes the operative fiducial
   383	    bound from primary evidence, and memoizes every in-memory member
   384	    re-reduction.  It never persists or substitutes a summary artifact.
   385	    The ledger boundary closes workflow omission, unregistered evidence, and
   386	    rollback/stale-head consumption; it does not defend against a malicious
   387	    trusted writer or a rewrite of both Git and full ledger history.
   388	    """
   389	
   390	    def __init__(
   391	        self,
   392	        runs_root: Path,
   393	        referenced_bundle_ids: set[str],
   394	        *,
   395	        evaluation_basis_sha256: str | None = None,
   396	        consumption_semantics_id: str = MAX_BRACKET_CONSUMPTION_SEMANTICS_ID,
   397	        calibration_ledger_snapshot: CalibrationLedgerSnapshot | None = None,
   398	        _allow_unissued_calibration_fixture: bool = False,
   399	    ) -> None:
   400	        if consumption_semantics_id not in {
   401	            MINTED_CONSUMPTION_SEMANTICS_ID,
   402	            MAX_BRACKET_CONSUMPTION_SEMANTICS_ID,
   403	            SALVAGE_DANGLER_CONSUMPTION_SEMANTICS_ID,
   404	        }:
   405	            raise ValueError(
   406	                f"unknown whole-window consumption semantics: {consumption_semantics_id!r}"
   407	            )
   408	        self.runs_root = Path(runs_root)
   409	        self.referenced_bundle_ids = frozenset(referenced_bundle_ids)
   410	        self.evaluation_basis_sha256 = evaluation_basis_sha256
   411	        self.consumption_semantics_id = consumption_semantics_id
   412	        self.calibration_ledger_snapshot = calibration_ledger_snapshot
   413	        self._allow_unissued_calibration_fixture = (
   414	            _allow_unissued_calibration_fixture
   415	        )
   416	        if self.calibration_ledger_snapshot is None:
   417	            acceptance = load_calibration_acceptance_bound()
   418	            cutoff = (
   419	                acceptance.get("ledger_cutoff")
   420	                if isinstance(acceptance, Mapping)
   421	                else None
   422	            )
   423	            self.calibration_ledger_snapshot = load_calibration_ledger_snapshot(
   424	                baseline_sequence=(
   425	                    cutoff.get("sequence") if isinstance(cutoff, Mapping) else None
   426	                ),
   427	                baseline_digest=(
   428	                    cutoff.get("head_digest") if isinstance(cutoff, Mapping) else None
   429	                ),
   430	            )
   431	        self.calibration_bracket: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None
   432	        self.operative_fiducial_bound_s: float | None = None
   433	        self.refusal_reasons: tuple[str, ...] = ()
   434	        self.path_refusal_reasons: dict[
   435	            str,
   436	            dict[tuple[str, ...], tuple[str, ...]],
   437	        ] = {}
   438	        self._prepared = False
   439	        self._preparation_identity: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] | None = None
   440	        self._summaries: dict[str, Mapping[str, Any]] = {}
   441	        self._provenance: dict[str, Mapping[str, Any]] = {}
   442	        self._row_validation_results: dict[
   443	            tuple[str, str, tuple[str, ...], str | None],
   444	            tuple[bool, tuple[str, ...]],
   445	        ] = {}
   446	
   447	    @property
   448	    def ready(self) -> bool:
   449	        return self._prepared and not self.refusal_reasons
   450	
   451	    def _fail_global(self, reasons: set[str] | tuple[str, ...]) -> None:
   452	        """Clear every authenticated cache when any global refusal exists."""
   453	
   454	        self._summaries.clear()
   455	        self._provenance.clear()
   456	        self.path_refusal_reasons.clear()
   457	        self._row_validation_results.clear()
   458	        self.refusal_reasons = tuple(
   459	            sorted(
   460	                set(reasons)
   461	                or {"whole_window_verdict_provenance_invalid"}
   462	            )
   463	        )
   464	
   465	    def _prepare(
   466	        self,
   467	        *,
   468	        bundle_paths: Mapping[str, Path],
   469	        policy: CampaignPolicy,
   470	    ) -> None:
   471	        identity = tuple(
   472	            sorted(
   473	                (bundle_id, str(Path(path).resolve()))
   474	                for bundle_id, path in bundle_paths.items()
   475	            )
   476	        )
   477	        if self._prepared:

  3836	def _validated_evaluation_basis(

## D-102: CAL-BRACKET-D079-01 pins ratified — corpus-derived budget cap, identity-epoch freshness, never-zero allowance, decimal numeric semantics

- Date: 2026-08-01
- Status: accepted (magistrate ratification after the two-round Sol xhigh
  design consult + the independent n=19 corpus reconstruction; ALL
  arithmetic lead-replayed at the bench: ceiling, cap, t(0.995,18)
  quantile by numerical CDF, window B pre-cal value against primary
  evidence bytes)
- Applies to: CAL-BRACKET-D079-01, the future
  `configs/calibration/calibration_acceptance_d079_v2.json` artifact

The four pins D-079 left unexecutable, now pinned:

1. **Budget cap (Candidate A, 99% two-draw prediction family, derived
   blind from the pre-window-B n=19 corpus):**
   `max_budgetable_excess_s = 0.001275166090593858`;
   `maximum_budgetable_drift_s = 0.012093166090593858`
   (= t(0.995,18)=2.878440472713585 × sd 0.002970761365307205 × √2;
   cap = ceiling − operative screen 0.010818). Consequences verified: a
   ~11.58 ms drift branch is budgetable; a 15 ms bracket refuses.
   **Window B itself remains refused regardless** — its pre-calibration
   0.035435840879704805 s (verified in primary evidence) exceeds the
   pre-flight level screen, and D-079 cl.2's systematic failure is
   never budgetable. The CAL-BRACKET regression at ~11 ms models the
   DRIFT BRANCH only, never a whole-window B pass.
2. **Freshness = exact identity epoch, no calendar hard expiry:** the
   artifact binds {os_build, hardware_model, power_policy,
   sampling_interval_ms, estimator_revision, pulse_protocol_id}; any
   change → `calibration_acceptance_bound_stale`. Mandatory prospective
   re-derivation triggers: any identity-field change; protocol/estimator
   byte change; a new valid same-identity calibration expanding the
   observed range; corpus doubling (19→38); a new systematic failure
   challenging the pre-flight screen. A trigger observation is judged
   under the PRIOR artifact — never incorporated into a threshold that
   judges itself. Calendar-age fields are provenance/advisory only (the
   corpus spans four days; a calendar constant would be invented).
3. **Never-zero allowance confirmed:**
   `A_s = max(observed_drift_s, 0.010818)`;
   `B_operative = max(B_pre, B_post) + A_s`, embedded ONCE in the
   authenticated operative fiducial bound (anchor-envelope
   re-reduction); no second calibration-drift energy term anywhere
   downstream (D-078 cl.11 single-count).
4. **Decimal numeric semantics:** the artifact stores source decimal
   lexemes and exact-decimal derivations (range
   0.010817749309353528 s; 95% prediction 0.008826584887500717 s;
   pre-flight exact max 0.03355875667989999 s) SEPARATELY from the
   ratified operative comparators (0.010818; 0.033558756679900;
   ROUND_HALF_EVEN at the declared quantum), hashing the decimal
   strings + rounding rule into the derivation sha256. D-079's
   12-place `0.010817749309` is a LABELLED presentation value, never a
   comparator. Acceptance comparisons run in decimal semantics;
   binary64 conversion happens only at the reducer boundary and is
   recorded.

Corpus provenance: the n=19 member list with per-member manifest and
evidence sha256s is reconstructed and lead-spot-verified (2026-08-01
session records; summary in the session custody dir) — the artifact
copies those tables verbatim with re-verification at authoring, never
retyped. Implementation remains sequenced behind gauntlet commit 3 and
the D-100 repair (shared write surfaces).

Revisit when: CAL-BRACKET-D079-01's delta audit reports, or any
re-derivation trigger fires.

## D-110: Mint 1 retroactively NON-CLAIM-BEARING (taint-and-remint); RT-2 dependency edge minted; the night consult's 7B-mint license SUSPENDED

> **2026-08-07 supersession (D-117):** clause 3's historical re-mint
> order is SUPERSEDED — structurally unsatisfiable at main (see
> `docs/process_traces/2026-08-06-d110-remint-fork/`); replaced by
> three prospective windows. The taint holding and the never-zero
> allowance correction STAND and bind the D-117 mints.

- Date: 2026-08-03 (Ed ruling, present, option "taint-and-remint" selected
  from the magistrate's three-option packet during the 16h runway)
- Status: accepted (trigger: the Ed-ordered two-week read-only soundness
  sweep — 34 agents, Fable auditors + Sol xhigh second-eyes, run in a
  parallel session — finding RT-1, Sol-confirmed. Memory record:
  two-week-soundness-sweep-2026-08-03; full results ephemeral in that
  session's task outputs.)
- Applies to: `df-ph-decode-floor-mint1` (absolute 3.592138 /
  comparative 7.377086 / operative gate 7.377086 J), row
  MINT-GENERALIZE-01, CLAIMS_STATUS, the D-095 chain.

**Grounds (RT-1):** mint #1's consumed fiducial bounds embed a
never-zero allowance of ZERO where D-102 pin 3 mandates
+max(drift, 0.010818 s) — for a10 a ~+43% wider operative bound than the
7.377086 J floor was derived from. The CAL-BRACKET-D079-01 adjudication
record framed the defect as a non-salvage severity escalator
(mis-refusals only); the accepted-side, anti-conservative direction was
never ruled on. RT-5 (recorded): all four PASSED window verdicts are
UNTAINTED — the 0.010 cliff is strictly tighter than the ruled screen
(drifts 8-25x below it) and the 10-field identity match supersets the
D-102 epoch; the taint is confined to floor artifacts.

**Ruling:**
1. Mint #1 is retroactively NON-CLAIM-BEARING. No consumption, quotation
   as a claim, or gating use of its floors until re-mint. Per
   CLAIMS_STATUS no landed claim has consumed it; if any consumption is
   discovered it voids with it.
2. RE-MINT CONDITIONS: (a) the D-109 CAL-BRACKET implementation lands
   (merged + gauntlet-clean); (b) the acceptance artifact is ISSUED
   (R2 backfill verified, ledger bootstrapped, head pinned); (c) the
   library validator's evidence_root_id pin is widened by scheduled work
   (DC-2/FM-3) so minted artifacts authenticate truthfully; then mint #1
   re-derives under the landed selector with the computed allowance.
3. RT-2 dependency edge MINTED in the kernel: MINT-GENERALIZE-01 is
   hard-blocked on CAL-BRACKET-D079-01 landing + this ruling's re-mint
   conditions. The 2026-08-03 night consult's Q3 license (governed 7B
   mint after byte-compare) is SUSPENDED as superseded-by-evidence —
   recorded honestly: the joint consult licensed it without RT-1 in
   frame because the adjudication record itself understated the defect's
   direction.
4. The Q1 mint-1 byte-compare replay REMAINS licensed (verification of
   tooling parity + the FM-1/FM-2 re-derivability question; it creates
   no claim). Its result is recorded either way.

## D-111: Adjudication evidence gains tracked custody — docs/process_traces/ is the home; .desk is working scratch only

- Date: 2026-08-03 (Ed ruling, present; option "track adjudication
  evidence" selected)
- Status: accepted (trigger: the soundness sweep's strongest structural
  finding — six domains independently: load-bearing adjudication
  evidence exists only in untracked `.desk/` — cold-gate packets and
  rulings, the D-108 debate record, the gate-3 synthesis CLAIMS_STATUS
  cites, the TEST-SPEED timing corpus, archive manifest digests — while
  the project's whole pivot is custody and attestation.)
- Applies to: all future adjudication artifacts; a named backfill set.

**Ruling:**
1. Going forward, LOAD-BEARING adjudication artifacts — cold-gate
   packets and rulings, refuter reports, debate/consult records that a
   decision entry cites, digest-bound re-records, decision-input
   corpora (e.g. timing data), archive manifest digests — are committed
   under `docs/process_traces/` (dated subdirectories) in the same
   session that produces them. A decision entry may not cite a memo as
   authority unless it is tracked or explicitly declared ephemeral in
   the entry itself.
2. `.desk/` remains legitimate working scratch; nothing load-bearing
   terminates there.
3. BACKFILL (this session): the D-100/D100-BII cold-gate packets and
   rulings (`.desk/coldgate_d100_bii/`, `.desk/adjudication_packet_20260801/`),
   the D-108/D-109 debate record, the night-consult rulings memo, the
   clause-(d) re-record JSON, the CAL-BRACKET F3 memos
   (`.desk/calbracket_d079/`), the TEST-SPEED timing corpus
   (`.desk/test-speed-consult/`, `.desk/testspeed/`), and the archive
   manifest digests (RS-4). Large or binary members may be represented
   by a digest manifest with the bytes retained in `.desk` + backup.

   (`native_intersection_empty`) + downstream environment-admission

   without it) and per-bundle attribution with a stage-1-clean

   sub-branch remains unpinned (open sub-question in the record).

   re-collection), the refuter-F7 scope question (whether one member of

   the fresh NEG-8 bound re-mint that any future licensed run needs
   (the 2026-08-01 bound expired 2026-08-02; recorded against the
   magistrate's packet as an omission).
5. STANDING CORRECTION (both instruments): condition spellings are
   NON-UNIQUE to producer — `environment_admission_missing` has a
   window-level cascade producer AND a per-bundle reduce-time producer.
   D-100's cascade classification was correct for the producer it

## D-109 addendum II: reviewed mint-core interface amendment (integration-collision resolution); D-110 oracle clarification

- Date: 2026-08-04 (successor magistrate ruling after bounded
  pre-decision Sol high consult, one round; Ed's HIGH effort cap
  observed)
- Status: executed (PR #100 gate-complete, CI green at `4280ebd`;
  merge is Ed's tap — the harness denies agent self-merge)
- Record: `docs/process_traces/2026-08-04-calbracket-integration-collision/`
  (FINDING.md, RESOLUTION.md, impl + delta re-audit reports) and
  `docs/process_traces/2026-08-04-calbracket-collision-consult/`

1. D-109 R1.4's `calibration_ledger_snapshot` threading is a DELIBERATE
   REVIEWED INTERFACE REVISION of the mint core. The generalized mint's
   `_CORE_SIGNATURES` pin is amended to the new signature; no adapter
   shim, no multi-version pin, no core-file digest pin (consult Q1,
   adopted). Future `_CORE_SIGNATURES` changes require explicit
   signature-pin review plus parity evidence (noted in-code).
2. The guard's framing is corrected to REVIEW-PINNED MINT-CORE
   INTERFACE — it pins selected signatures of a review-controlled core
   file and is not a byte freeze; "byte-identical" is reserved for
   observed output comparisons.
3. D-110 CLARIFICATION (conditions unchanged): tooling byte-identity
   evidence means INTEGRATION-TREE CORE-VS-WRAPPER PARITY on identical
   inputs. It does not require any future artifact to match the tainted
   historical mint-1 digests — D-110's corrected re-mint may
   legitimately produce different bytes. MINT-GENERALIZE-01's
   acceptance evidence is reworded accordingly in the kernel.
4. Guard hardening (delta re-audit F2, proven live): rendered-signature
   comparison is spoofable by a default whose `repr()` is `None`; the
   guard now identity-checks the None sentinel defaults structurally,
   with a regression. Residual honestly held: `__signature__` spoofing
   remains a property of the approach; the guard is a reviewed-drift
   tripwire, not a security boundary against an adversarial core file.
5. PROCESS FINDING (candidate rule, NOT ratified here — rule-11
   cold-gate packet item): the lead's rule-1 verification replay runs
   on the INTEGRATION tree whenever the branch is behind main. Recorded
   with the collision as its motivating catch (CI on the merge ref was
   the only layer that could see it).

   109	def _canonical_sha256(value: Mapping[str, Any]) -> str:
   110	    raw = json.dumps(
   350	
   351	    statistics = derivation.get("source_statistics")
   352	    rounding = derivation.get("rounding")
   353	    operatives = derivation.get("ratified_operatives")
   354	    if not all(isinstance(item, Mapping) for item in (statistics, rounding, operatives)):
   355	        return False
   356	    with localcontext() as context:
   357	        context.prec = 80
   358	        count = Decimal(len(values))
   359	        mean = sum(values, Decimal(0)) / count
   360	        sample_sd = (
   361	            sum((item - mean) ** 2 for item in values) / Decimal(len(values) - 1)
   362	        ).sqrt()
   363	        quantum = Decimal("0.000000000000000001")
   364	        expected_statistics = {
   365	            "minimum_s": str(min(values)),
   366	            "maximum_s": str(max(values)),
   367	            "range_s": str(max(values) - min(values)),
   368	            "mean_presentation_s": str(
   369	                mean.quantize(quantum, rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN)
   370	            ),
   371	            "sample_sd_presentation_s": str(
   372	                sample_sd.quantize(quantum, rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN)
   373	            ),
   374	        }
   375	    minimum_id = member_ids[values.index(min(values))]
   376	    maximum_id = member_ids[values.index(max(values))]
   377	    if (
   378	        statistics.get("minimum_s") != expected_statistics["minimum_s"]
   379	        or statistics.get("maximum_s") != expected_statistics["maximum_s"]
   380	        or statistics.get("range_s") != expected_statistics["range_s"]
   381	        or statistics.get("minimum_member_id") != minimum_id
   382	        or statistics.get("maximum_member_id") != maximum_id
   383	        or not isinstance(statistics.get("mean_presentation_s"), Mapping)
   384	        or statistics["mean_presentation_s"].get("value")
   385	        != expected_statistics["mean_presentation_s"]
   386	        or statistics["mean_presentation_s"].get("label")
   387	        != "rounded_presentation"
   388	        or not isinstance(statistics.get("sample_sd_presentation_s"), Mapping)
   389	        or statistics["sample_sd_presentation_s"].get("value")
   390	        != expected_statistics["sample_sd_presentation_s"]
   391	        or statistics["sample_sd_presentation_s"].get("label")
   392	        != "rounded_presentation"
   393	        or statistics.get("prediction_95_two_draw_s")
   394	        != "0.008826584887500717"
   395	        or statistics.get("prediction_99_two_draw_s")
   396	        != "0.012093166090593858"
   397	        or rounding.get("mode") != "ROUND_HALF_EVEN"
   398	        or not isinstance(rounding.get("operative_bracket_screen"), Mapping)
   399	        or rounding["operative_bracket_screen"].get("quantum_s") != "0.000001"
   400	        or rounding["operative_bracket_screen"].get("value_s")
   401	        != _D102_OPERATIVE_VALUES["bracket_screen_s"]
   402	        or not isinstance(rounding.get("preflight_level_screen"), Mapping)
   403	        or rounding["preflight_level_screen"].get("quantum_s")
   404	        != "0.000000000000001"
   405	        or rounding["preflight_level_screen"].get("value_s")
   406	        != _D102_OPERATIVE_VALUES["preflight_level_screen_s"]
   407	        or any(operatives.get(key) != item for key, item in _D102_OPERATIVE_VALUES.items())
   408	        or operatives.get("allowance_rule")
   409	        != "max(observed_drift_s,bracket_screen_s)"
   410	        or operatives.get("operative_bound_rule")
   411	        != "max(pre_b_fiducial_s,post_b_fiducial_s)+calibration_drift_allowance_s"
   412	        or operatives.get("embedding_count") != 1
   413	    ):
   414	        return False
   415	    screen = Decimal(_D102_OPERATIVE_VALUES["bracket_screen_s"])
   416	    maximum = Decimal(_D102_OPERATIVE_VALUES["maximum_budgetable_drift_s"])
   417	    excess = Decimal(_D102_OPERATIVE_VALUES["max_budgetable_excess_s"])
   418	    return (
   419	        (max(values) - min(values)).quantize(
   420	            Decimal("0.000001"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN
   421	        )
   422	        == screen
   423	        and max(values).quantize(
   424	            Decimal("0.000000000000001"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN
   425	        )
   426	        == Decimal(_D102_OPERATIVE_VALUES["preflight_level_screen_s"])
   427	        and screen + excess == maximum
   428	    )

docs/paper/related_work_draft.md:3:JouleWise lies at the intersection of inference-energy benchmarking, software power measurement, experimental metrology, and split inference. Its central difference is one of emphasis: the measurement instrument is the product, while model and deployment comparisons are demonstration studies. The instrument reports an energy verdict for a complete, declared measurement window; records the raw observations and their chain of custody; freezes the comparison and acceptance rules before seeing the result; and declines to make a claim when an effect falls below its detection floor, the smallest effect it can distinguish under the stated conditions. This framing makes uncertainty, timing attribution, drift, and evidence integrity part of the result rather than implementation details behind a leaderboard value.
docs/paper/related_work_draft.md:17:JouleWise applies this lineage to `powermetrics` on Apple silicon. It integrates named system-on-chip power channels only inside runtime-emitted phase boundaries, retains the raw counter stream, and calibrates timing attribution inside the same experimental window. Its current validated characterization finds that assigning power samples to the correct phase contributes about one joule of uncertainty and dominates ordinary repeat-to-repeat variation. In plain terms, the limiting question is not whether the machine repeats the workload consistently, but whether samples near a phase boundary belong just inside or just outside it. <!-- CLAIMS_STATUS.md section 1: the VALID standing measurement fact is that the instrument is attribution-limited at approximately one joule, rather than noise-limited. --> This limitation is published as part of the detection floor. It is not hidden by a smooth average or treated as a constant calibration offset.
scripts/extract_detection_floors.py:16:never publishes a claim-bearing floor from them.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md:9:We argue that a software power counter should be treated as a scientific instrument rather than as a logging convenience. The instrument must be calibrated in the same session in which it is used; each reported result must carry a detection floor, meaning the smallest false effect that the calibrated method could plausibly produce under the stated conditions; and the analysis must decline a directional claim when the observed effect cannot clear that floor and its own measurement uncertainty. JouleWise implements this discipline for phase-resolved, single-request LLM inference on one named Apple-silicon machine and software stack. The runtime emits the phase boundaries because it drives the workload, while `powermetrics` supplies the power samples integrated between those boundaries.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md:54:The pre- and post-window calibrations form a bracket around the measurements. Both must be authenticated, fresh, and causally outside the science interval. The operative bound is the larger of the two. Separately, the absolute difference between the pre- and post-window calibrations is screened against a derived bracket-drift limit of about 10.82 ms: a small repeatability-only excess is propagated into every floor and claim, while an identified systematic defect cannot be absorbed by that budget. If the post-window bound is larger than the one used when a member was first reduced, the member must be re-reduced through the pre-specified path with the wider bound or it cannot support a claim; metadata is never patched to make the bounds agree. A pre-flight level screen also runs before the first science member. It rejects a calibration whose fitted lag is outside the previously characterized family, such as a graphics-processor frequency ramp that the pulse model could mistake for a timing shift. A retry is allowed only after a specific cause is identified and removed, within the retry count frozen before collection. Repeating merely until a favorable calibration appears would be selection on the outcome.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md:60:A *detection floor* is a practical guard against false observed effects for one declared condition family: the same telemetry backend, metric, window type, workload profile, and stack identity. One such family forms a measurement cell. The floor is not a claim that a population percentile has been estimated exactly. JouleWise computes separate absolute and comparative floors and takes their maximum for the cell. An absolute floor measures how far repeated measurements of the same condition wander from their mean. A comparative floor measures the apparent difference between labels that are deliberately made identical and collected in A/B/B/A order.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md:109:The floor is only one side of a claim decision. The calibrated floor bounds a false effect produced by the calibration condition; the confidence or decision interval for the particular measured contrast separately carries that contrast's timing-attribution uncertainty. These are distinct uses of the same physical uncertainty and both are required. The effective bar is therefore
docs/paper/draft-v1.md:115:where \(B_{\mathrm{claim}}\) is the claim-side measurement bound. For the measured phase-contrast regime, this combined bar is approximately 5 J. Neither term may be removed as an apparent double count. Effects below the floor are reported as *not resolvable*, not as zero, equal, or evidence of no difference. A directional claim is made only when the effect and its interval clear the applicable bar.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md:137:The custody chain continues after collection. The immutable corpus is backed up before extraction. The extractor re-authenticates member hashes, required files and cross-file consistency, calibration identity, environment admission, complete campaign membership, cooldown evidence, phase metric identity, and the whole-window drift allowance. It excludes or refuses a cell according to the frozen rules; missing uncertainty never becomes zero. The current artifact boundary is stated honestly: until floor artifacts are independently bound to their source extraction, a claim-bearing floor must be produced by protocol-controlled extraction in the same controlled custody session as the analysis that consumes it. A standalone floor file is not independently claim-licensing.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md:139:The refusal log is part of the evaluation, not an embarrassment to omit. It records contaminated members, out-of-family calibration, stale drift evidence, unresolved clock anchors, duplicate occurrences, and below-floor effects. In one real end-of-night case, the governed re-evaluation refused a window because a member's internal clock alignment could not be resolved. Independent adjudication found that refusal correct. The result remained non-claim-bearing: an example of the fail-closed design working as intended, not a software defect to be bypassed.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md:143:Instrument characterization asks whether the complete measurement system behaves predictably when driven by signals whose qualitative answer is known in advance. The workload is therefore a test signal, not yet the scientific finding. All tests retain the same calibration, admission, custody, and floor rules as the later demonstration measurements. Existing campaign fragments are not promoted where the governing whole-window verdict did not pass; the table marks the required claim-bearing results explicitly.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md:166:This section will report phase-resolved gross joules per request for two model sizes, with tokenizer-scoped joules per prompt token and per output token as companion metrics. It will contain the pre-registered same-boundary model-size contrast, its interval, the complete floor decomposition, the claim-side bound, the effect-to-floor ratio, and the final resolvable/unresolved verdict. No demonstration energy value from the superseded mint is carried into this draft. A quantization ladder will be included only if it is collected under its own stack-specific floors and the frozen window budget permits it.
docs/paper/draft-v1.md:194:JouleWise does not claim a new split scheduler in this paper. Split inference is instead a demanding future demonstration of the instrument because it introduces two physical boundaries, a transfer interval, and clock alignment across devices. A valid comparison would have to measure both ends, name each boundary, and clear a pre-registered floor or calibrated bridge. Whether splitting saves energy remains an empirical outcome; the reusable contribution is a method that can issue, qualify, or refuse the result.
docs/paper/draft-v1-review-round1.md:115:That max rule is correct, but it omits a distinct part of the current method. Bracket drift is the absolute pre/post difference and is screened against the derived 10.817749309 ms limit. A slight repeatability-only excess is propagated into every floor and claim; an identified systematic defect cannot be absorbed by that budget. Sources: `docs/phase_2/detection_floor.md:757-783`; `docs/phase_2/window_runbook.md:701-728`.

A key distinction has emerged: there is already a generalized wrapper, but it does not replace the old mint core—it monkey-patches the core’s constants from a supplied pinset and guards selected function signatures. I’m checking whether that wrapper truly closes every old literal/CLI/root assumption and whether downstream analysis authenticates the resulting new-family artifact.

   180	def _object(
   181	    value: object,
   182	    label: str,
   183	    expected_keys: set[str],
   184	) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
   185	    if not isinstance(value, Mapping):
   186	        raise MintError(f"{label} must be an object")
   187	    keys = set(value)
   188	    missing = sorted(expected_keys - keys)
   189	    extra = sorted(keys - expected_keys)
   190	    if missing or extra:
   191	        details = []
   192	        if missing:
   193	            details.append(f"missing={missing}")
   194	        if extra:
   195	            details.append(f"extra={extra}")
   196	        raise MintError(f"{label} schema mismatch: {'; '.join(details)}")
   197	    return value
   198	
   199	
   200	def _string(value: object, label: str) -> str:
   201	    if not isinstance(value, str) or not value or value != value.strip():
   202	        raise MintError(f"{label} must be a nonempty trimmed string")
   203	    return value
   204	
   205	
   206	def _evidence_root_id(value: object, label: str) -> str:
   207	    text = _string(value, label)
   208	    if _EVIDENCE_ROOT_ID_RE.fullmatch(text) is None:
   209	        raise MintError(
   210	            f"{label} must be a portable identifier containing only letters, "
   211	            "digits, dot, underscore, or hyphen"
   212	        )
   213	    return text
   214	
   215	
   216	def _sha256(value: object, label: str) -> str:
   217	    text = _string(value, label)
   218	    if _SHA256_RE.fullmatch(text) is None:
   219	        raise MintError(f"{label} must be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters")
   220	    return text
   221	
   222	
   223	def _positive_int(value: object, label: str) -> int:
   224	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int) or value <= 0:
   225	        raise MintError(f"{label} must be a positive integer")
   226	    return value
   227	
   228	
   229	def _nonnegative_number(value: object, label: str) -> float:
   230	    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int | float):
   231	        raise MintError(f"{label} must be a finite nonnegative number")
   232	    converted = float(value)
   233	    if not math.isfinite(converted) or converted < 0.0:
   234	        raise MintError(f"{label} must be a finite nonnegative number")
   235	    return converted
